### 15.8 Procedure — Update Existing Content Without Breaking User Data


Use case: fixing a typo, adding a missed risk factor, correcting a wrong rationale.

#### 15.8.1 Safe changes (no user data impact)

These can be made freely:
- Text content within sections
- HTML formatting changes that don't alter IDs
- CSS adjustments
- Adding new abbreviations
- Adding new mid-reads (they're inline)
- Adding new condition-blocks within an existing section
- Adding new finding-cards within a condition-block

#### 15.8.2 Changes that affect user data

These need extra care:

**Changing a chapter ID** (`ch5` → `ch5b`):
- Old key `progress.ch5: 2` becomes orphan
- User loses "read" status for that chapter
- **Mitigation:** include a migration in Book load script:
  ```javascript
  (function migrateChapterIds() {
    var p = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('nur2460_atimn_progress') || '{}');
    var migrations = { 'ch5': 'ch5b' };
    var changed = false;
    Object.keys(migrations).forEach(function(oldId) {
      if (oldId in p) {
        p[migrations[oldId]] = p[oldId];
        delete p[oldId];
        changed = true;
      }
    });
    if (changed) localStorage.setItem('nur2460_atimn_progress', JSON.stringify(p));
  })();
  ```

**Changing a section ID within a chapter** (`ch5-nutrition` → `ch5-diet`):
- Bookmarks pointing to the old section ID won't open
- **Mitigation:** add to bookmark migration:
  ```javascript
  (function migrateBookmarkIds() {
    var b = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('nur2460_bookmarks') || '[]');
    var migrations = { 'ch5-nutrition': 'ch5-diet' };
    var changed = false;
    b.forEach(function(bm) {
      if (bm.sectionId in migrations) {
        bm.sectionId = migrations[bm.sectionId];
        changed = true;
      }
    });
    if (changed) localStorage.setItem('nur2460_bookmarks', JSON.stringify(b));
  })();
  ```

**Removing or renaming a flashcard prompt** (`ch5-p1` removed):
- Schedule entry for that ID becomes orphan
- User's review history is "lost" for that prompt
- **Mitigation:** option 1 — leave it (orphans don't break anything); option 2 — purge:
  ```javascript
  (function purgeRemovedPrompts() {
    var validIds = new Set();
    Object.keys(MID_PROMPTS).forEach(function(ch) {
      MID_PROMPTS[ch].forEach(function(p) { validIds.add(p.id); });
    });
    // Also add inline mid-read IDs
    document.querySelectorAll('.mid-read[data-fc-id]').forEach(function(el) {
      validIds.add(el.dataset.fcId);
    });
    var s = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('nur2460_fc_schedule') || '{}');
    Object.keys(s).forEach(function(id) {
      if (!validIds.has(id)) delete s[id];
    });
    localStorage.setItem('nur2460_fc_schedule', JSON.stringify(s));
  })();
  ```

**Removing a template** (an `ex-chN-{name}` deleted):
- `nur2460_atimnTemplates_progress` has stale entry
- Pickup panel might point to non-existent ID
- **Mitigation:** purge studied entries for removed IDs:
  ```javascript
  (function purgeRemovedTemplates() {
    var validIds = new Set();
    document.querySelectorAll('.example-card[id^="ex-"]').forEach(function(el) {
      validIds.add(el.id);
    });
    var s = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('nur2460_atimnTemplates_progress') || '{}');
    Object.keys(s).forEach(function(id) {
      if (!validIds.has(id)) delete s[id];
    });
    localStorage.setItem('nur2460_atimnTemplates_progress', JSON.stringify(s));
  })();
  ```

#### 15.8.3 Migration script template

```javascript
// Place inside Book Script 1 (Main IIFE), before DOMContentLoaded listener
(function runDataMigrations() {
  var MIGRATION_VERSION_KEY = 'nur2460_atimn_migration_version';
  var current = parseInt(localStorage.getItem(MIGRATION_VERSION_KEY) || '0', 10);
  var migrations = [
    // Version 1: rename ch5-nutrition section
    function v1() {
      var b = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('nur2460_bookmarks') || '[]');
      b.forEach(function(bm) {
        if (bm.sectionId === 'ch5-nutrition') bm.sectionId = 'ch5-diet';
      });
      localStorage.setItem('nur2460_bookmarks', JSON.stringify(b));
    },
    // Version 2: purge orphan flashcards
    function v2() {
      // ... migration logic
    }
  ];
  for (var v = current; v < migrations.length; v++) {
    try {
      migrations[v]();
      localStorage.setItem(MIGRATION_VERSION_KEY, String(v + 1));
    } catch(e) {
      console.warn('Migration v' + (v + 1) + ' failed:', e);
      break;
    }
  }
})();
```

This pattern lets you ship migrations safely — each user runs them once.

##### 15.9.3.5 Ch5 dual-content note (v3 cleanup)

Pharm ch5 (Adverse Effects, Interactions, and Contraindications) was originally extracted with **two complete content sets** from the source PDF — same chapter authored twice with different emphases. Earlier work renamed duplicate IDs to be unique but left H2 headings duplicated. v3 cleanup renamed the H2s to disambiguate. The two halves were intentionally preserved (both contribute unique content):

**First half** (sections in document order):
1. ch5-tldr (TL;DR · One-glance summary)
2. ch5-types ("Types of Adverse Reactions — Overview")
3. ch5-anaphylaxis ("Anaphylaxis — Recognition and Response")
4. ch5-interactions ("Drug Interactions — Mechanisms")
5. ch5-pregnancy ("Pregnancy and Lactation Considerations")
6. ch5-als ("Active Learning Scenario · Gentamicin + Naproxen")
7. ch5-exercises ("Practice · Application Exercises (Set 1)" — 5 NCLEX questions)

**Second half** (supplementary content):
8. ch5-reactions ("Adverse Reactions — Common Patterns")
9. ch5-special ("Serious & Special Reactions" — SJS/TEN, Black Box, Teratogenic)
10. ch5-interactions-2 ("Drug Interactions — CYP450 and Foods")
11. ch5-als-2 ("Active Learning Scenario · Warfarin + St. John's Wort")
12. ch5-exercises-2 ("Practice · Application Exercises (Set 2)" — 5 more NCLEX questions)

ch5 inline mid-reads (5 cards) anchor to `ch5-tldr` and draw from BOTH halves' content:
- fc-ch5-anaphylaxis-first-line, fc-ch5-biphasic-monitor → from first half
- fc-ch5-sjs-culprits, fc-ch5-cyp450-inducers, fc-ch5-cyp450-inhibitors-grapefruit → from second half

##### 15.9.3.6 Pharm inline mid-read density (v3 retrospective)

162 inline mid-reads across all 49 chapters, **variable density** by content richness:

| Density | Card count | Chapters |
|---|---|---|
| Heavy | 4–5 each | ch5, ch9, ch10, ch13, ch14, ch19, ch20, ch21, ch23, ch25, ch27, ch28, ch32, ch35, ch39, ch43, ch44, ch47 (18 chapters) |
| Standard | 3 each | most chapters (25) |
| Light | 2 each | ch3, ch17, ch29, ch30, ch38, ch49 (6 chapters) |

**Why variable density (not the flat 3-per-chapter of the MN model):** Pharm content is heterogeneous — ch5 (adverse effects) alone justifies 5 distinct safety cards; ch3 (dosage calc) has 2 useful formulas and not much else. Flat density would underuse rich chapters and force filler in thin ones. SM-2 mixes everything in the queue regardless, so uneven coverage doesn't disadvantage the student.

**Authoring pipeline (followed for sub-batches A–E, 33+30+34+33+29 cards):**
1. Extract each chapter's TL;DR text via Python script
2. Draft cards in JSON file (`pharm_inline_batch_X.json`) — one card = `{id, ch, type, anchor, q, a}`
3. Insert `<aside class="mid-read">` blocks into Pharm Book just before each chapter's closing `</section>` of `chN-tldr`
4. Append matching entries to STARTER_DECK in Pharm Flashcards (with comma-boundary check)
5. Validate: `node --check` on every script block; cross-file ID parity check

**Lesson from sub-batch A insertion bug:** When appending to a JS array literal, ALWAYS verify whether the last existing entry has a trailing comma. The Flashcards STARTER_DECK initially had no trailing comma; appending new entries on new lines without a separator produced two adjacent objects → JS SyntaxError → "Uncaught Error: Script error" → entire page broke. Fix is either (a) add the missing comma, (b) insert with leading comma, or (c) rewrite the array boundary explicitly. The pipeline now does an explicit boundary check before each insertion.

#### 15.9.4 Hub layout adaptation per subject

**Stats row:** always 5 stats. If a count is unknown (subject not finished), display "—" instead of 0.

**Units-grid:** auto-adapts via `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr))`.
- 3 units → single row of 3
- 4 units → single row of 4 (tight) or 2x2 on narrow screens
- 13 units → multiple rows (wrap)

**Types-grid:** always 8 rows (one per template type). 2-column on desktop, 1-column on mobile.

#### 15.9.5 Adapting the storage panel per subject

The Storage panel reads all keys matching the subject prefix. The prefix depends on subject:

```javascript
// MN Hub:
var PREFIX = 'nur2460_';   // shows MN-specific + shared keys

// PD Hub:
var PREFIX = 'atipd_';     // shows PD-specific keys only

// Pharm Hub:
var PREFIX = 'nur2460_';   // shows Pharm + shared keys (overlap with MN)
```

**Implication:** MN Hub and Pharm Hub both show overlapping keys in their storage panel. This is intentional — both subjects use the same shared keys for theme, bookmarks, flashcards.

**Resetting:** "Reset all progress" only clears keys matching the prefix. So:
- MN reset clears `nur2460_atimn_progress`, but NOT `nur2460_fc_schedule` (since the latter is shared)... unless the prefix check is just `'nur2460_'`, in which case it clears EVERYTHING with that prefix including Pharm's data.

**This is a known quirk** (Pharm shares `nur2460_fc_schedule` with MN — see §12 LocalStorage schema). Resetting MN may wipe Pharm flashcard progress because they share `nur2460_fc_schedule`. Users should export backup first.

#### 15.9.6 Per-subject Book Script 3 (mid-prompts) location

The mid-prompts script must be the LAST inline script in the Book, after the NCLEX filter script. Order in Book file:

```
<script>/* Main IIFE — 49 functions */</script>
<script>/* BATCH 3 NCLEX filter + answered tracking */</script>
<script>/* Mid-read flashcard prompts (MID_PROMPTS injection) */</script>
</body>
```

When building a new subject's Book, copy this script ORDER. Inverting it causes injectAllPrompts() to fire before buildPromptCard() is defined, throwing a ReferenceError.

#### 15.9.7 Cross-subject Flashcards strategy

**Current state (resolved — Option A shipped):**
- MN: `nur2460_fc_schedule` (shared)
- Pharm: `nur2460_fc_schedule` (shared — same key as MN)
- PD: `atipd_fc_schedule` (still separate; PD remains in its own namespace)

**The decision matrix that was considered:**

Option A — Shared schedule (MN+Pharm cards in one queue):
- Card IDs must be unambiguous across both subjects. ✅ This holds in our case:
  - MN uses `fc-chN-{semantic-slug}` (e.g., `fc-ch1-naegele`, `fc-ch1-spinnbarkeit`)
  - Pharm uses `fc-chN-pN` (e.g., `fc-ch11-p1`, `fc-ch11-p2`)
  - Verified: 0 ID overlap between MN (122 cards) and Pharm (98 cards)
- Separate Flashcards files each contribute to the same shared schedule.

Option B — Separate schedules:
- Pharm Flashcards uses `nur2460_atipharm_fc_schedule`
- No ID prefixing needed
- Two separate Flashcards files, two separate queues

**Chosen:** Option A — matches §15.7.3's rationale ("one queue across subjects studied in same week")
and matches MN's live implementation. The ID schemes were already non-colliding so no prefixing
was required. Earlier guide language preferring Option B is superseded by this section.

**For PD** — if you ever want to fold PD into the shared namespace, see §15.7.9 migration path
and additionally prefix PD card IDs (PD uses `fc-ch1-{slug}` which DOES collide with MN's pattern).

## PART 18 — CANONICAL ATI ACTIVE LEARNING TEMPLATES (REFERENCE)

Extracted verbatim from ATI Maternal Newborn Nursing Review Module Edition 11.0, appendix pages A1–A15. Every Templates file in this suite must conform to these 8 structures.

### 18.1 Basic Concept (A1)

**Header:** Concept · Review Module Chapter

**Sections (3 boxes):**
- Related Content (e.g., delegation, levels of prevention, advance directives)
- Underlying Principles
- Nursing Interventions (who? when? why? how?)

**Grid class:** `.bc-grid` (3 equal columns)

### 18.2 Diagnostic Procedure (A3)

**Header:** Procedure Name · Review Module Chapter

**Sections (7 boxes, with CONSIDERATIONS group):**
- Description of Procedure
- Indications
- **CONSIDERATIONS** (group):
  - Nursing Interventions (pre, intra, post)
  - Interpretation of Findings
  - Client Education
- Potential Complications  ←  Nursing Interventions  *(side-by-side with connector)*

**Grid class:** `.tp-grid` (shared with NS and TP)

**Key distinguishing heading:** **Interpretation of Findings** (DP only)

### 18.3 Growth and Development (A5)

**Header:** Developmental Stage · Review Module Chapter

**Sections (8 boxes in 2 groups):**
- **EXPECTED GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT** (group):
  - Physical Development
  - Cognitive Development
  - Psychosocial Development
  - Age-Appropriate Activities
- **HEALTH PROMOTION** (group):
  - Immunizations
  - Health Screening
  - Nutrition
  - Injury Prevention

**Grid class:** `.gd-grid` (NEW in v3 — added 2026-05-13)

### 18.4 Medication (A7)

**Header:** Medication · Review Module Chapter · **Category Class** · Purpose of Medication

**Sections (within "Purpose of Medication" group + body):**
- Expected Pharmacological Action  *(in Purpose group)*
- Therapeutic Use  *(in Purpose group)*
- Complications
- Medication Administration
- Contraindications/Precautions  *(no spaces around slash)*
- Nursing Interventions
- Interactions
- Client Education
- **Evaluation of Medication Effectiveness**

**Grid class:** `.med-grid`

### 18.5 Nursing Skill (A9)

**Header:** Skill Name · Review Module Chapter

**Sections (7 boxes, with CONSIDERATIONS group):**
- Description of Skill
- Indications
- Outcomes/Evaluation  *(no spaces)*
- **CONSIDERATIONS** (group):
  - Nursing Interventions (pre, intra, post)
  - Client Education
- Potential Complications  ←  Nursing Interventions  *(side-by-side with connector)*

**Grid class:** `.tp-grid` (shared with DP and TP)

### 18.6 System Disorder (A11)

**Header:** Disorder/Disease Process · Review Module Chapter

**Sections (14 boxes in 3 groups):**
- Top row (3 boxes spanning):
  - Alterations in Health (Diagnosis)
  - Pathophysiology Related to Client Problem
  - Health Promotion and Disease Prevention
- **ASSESSMENT** (group, 4 boxes):
  - Risk Factors
  - Expected Findings
  - Laboratory Tests
  - Diagnostic Procedures
- **SAFETY CONSIDERATIONS** (open shaded area + Complications inner box)
- **PATIENT-CENTERED CARE** (group, 5 boxes):
  - Nursing Care
  - Medications
  - Client Education
  - Therapeutic Procedures
  - Interprofessional Care

**Grid class:** `.sd-grid`

### 18.7 Therapeutic Procedure (A13)

**Header:** Procedure Name · Review Module Chapter

**Sections (7 boxes, with CONSIDERATIONS group):**
- Description of Procedure
- Indications
- **CONSIDERATIONS** (group):
  - Nursing Interventions (pre, intra, post)
  - Outcomes/Evaluation  *(no spaces)*
  - Client Education
- Potential Complications  ←  Nursing Interventions  *(side-by-side with connector)*

**Grid class:** `.tp-grid` (shared with DP and NS)

**Key distinguishing heading:** **Outcomes/Evaluation** (vs DP's "Interpretation of Findings")

### 18.8 Concept Analysis (A15)

**Header:** Concept Analysis

**Sections (5 boxes):**
- Defining Characteristics (full-width top)
- Antecedents *(what must occur/be in place for concept to exist/function properly)*
- Negative Consequences *(results from impaired antecedent — complete with faculty assistance)*
- Related Concepts *(review list of concepts and identify which can be affected by the status of this concept — complete with faculty assistance)*
- Exemplars

**Grid class:** `.ca-grid`

### 18.9 Common pitfalls (from v3 cleanup)

- **DP and TP have the same shape but different one heading**: DP uses "Interpretation of Findings" (you interpret results); TP uses "Outcomes/Evaluation" (you evaluate effectiveness). Never use a generic "Outcomes / Interpretation" merged label.
- **"Outcomes/Evaluation" and "Contraindications/Precautions" have NO spaces around the slash** in canonical ATI.
- **"Nursing Interventions" appears TWICE** in DP/NS/TP — once as `(pre, intra, post)` within the Considerations group, and once paired with Potential Complications. Both are required for full canonical compliance.
- **Medication header includes "Category Class"** — easy to omit.
- **Growth & Development is 8 boxes, not 3.** Don't merge Cognitive+Psychosocial or merge the 4 Health Promotion sections.
- **System Disorder Safety Considerations is an OPEN SHADED AREA**, not a labeled box like the others; the Complications box sits inside this safety area.

## PART 19 — TEMPLATE CANONICAL VISUAL COMPLIANCE — FIXES APPLIED

This section documents the per-template visual fixes applied during the final canonical compliance pass. The goal was to make each of the 8 ATI Active Learning Templates render as close to the canonical PDF as our theme system allows, while preserving study-tool features (Filled/Blank toggle, Worked Example label, source link).

### 19.0 Workflow — iterative per-template render-compare-fix loop

For each template type, the loop ran:

1. View canonical PNG from `/mnt/user-data/outputs/ATI_canonical_templates/`.
2. Render a representative card from MN, PD, or Pharm using Chrome headless (light theme, fixed viewport width).
3. Compare side-by-side. Identify specific visual or structural mismatches.
4. Apply fixes via Python regex on the HTML output files (CSS edits, HTML restructures).
5. Re-render and compare again. Iterate until visually approved.
6. Lock in the template type before moving to the next.

This avoided the brittleness of bulk-applying speculative fixes across all 369 template cards. Each CSS change was visually verified on at least one card per file before committing.

**Chrome headless render command pattern** (used throughout):

```bash
/home/claude/.cache/puppeteer/chrome/linux-131.0.6778.204/chrome-linux64/chrome \
  --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --hide-scrollbars \
  --window-size=WIDTHxHEIGHT \
  --screenshot=OUTPUT.png \
  file:///tmp/render.html
```

Where `/tmp/render.html` wraps an `.example-card` block with the full CSS extracted from the template file's `<style>` blocks, with `data-theme="light"` on the `<html>` element.

### 19.1 Basic Concept (A1) — APPROVED v1

**Canonical structure:** 3 boxes (Related Content, Underlying Principles, Nursing Interventions) in `.bc-grid`.

**Fixes applied:** None. The existing implementation matched canonical structure on first render. The only visible deviation is the absence of the gray "ACTIVE LEARNING TEMPLATE: Basic Concept" banner, which was an accepted trade-off across all template types.

**Accepted study-tool features (not in canonical):**
- "Worked Example" label
- Filled/Blank toggle button
- "Open chapter ↗" source link

### 19.2 Diagnostic Procedure (A3) — APPROVED v5

**Canonical structure:** Description of Procedure (full row), then 2-column layout — left has Indications, Interpretation of Findings, Potential Complications; right is the **CONSIDERATIONS** dark-wrapper group containing Nursing Interventions (pre, intra, post) + Client Education + Nursing Interventions. The two bottom boxes (Potential Complications and Nursing Interventions) are linked by a horizontal connector line.

#### 19.2.1 Box styling — the `.tp-grid > .tp-box` fix

**Symptom:** In the initial render, the boxes for Description of Procedure, Indications, Interpretation of Findings, Potential Complications, and Nursing Interventions had no visible borders or header strips — just plain headings followed by content. Only the CONSIDERATIONS group's children had proper styling.

**Cause:** The `.tp-grid > .description`, `.indications`, `.outcomes`, `.complications`, `.nursing-interventions` rules only set `grid-area`. There was no rule giving direct grid children the box styling that grouped-children (inside `.tp-grid > .considerations`) inherited.

**Fix:** Add a `.tp-grid > .tp-box` rule:

```css
.tp-grid > .tp-box {
  background: var(--surface);
  border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: 14px;
  /* NO overflow:hidden — would clip the connector pseudo-elements */
  padding: 0 !important;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
}
.tp-grid > .tp-box > h3 {
  background: var(--surface2);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-top-left-radius: 13px;
  border-top-right-radius: 13px;
  padding: 11px 16px;
  margin: 0;
  font-family: 'DM Serif Display', serif !important;
  font-weight: 400 !important;
  font-size: 15px !important;
  color: var(--text) !important;
  letter-spacing: 0 !important;
}
```

**Key constraint — no `overflow:hidden`:** Other box-styling rules in the codebase (`.bc-grid > .tp-box`, `.sd-grid > .tp-box`, etc.) use `overflow:hidden` to clip the h3's rectangular background to the box's rounded border. Here that would clip the connector pseudo-elements (`.complications::after`, `.nursing-interventions::before`) which extend outside the box bounds. Solution: clip the header strip by setting `border-top-left-radius` and `border-top-right-radius` on the h3 directly. The box bottom corners stay rounded because the content's background matches the box's background.

#### 19.2.2 Connector cleanup

The original CSS had **five** conflicting `.complications::after` / `.nursing-interventions::before` rules, including a `display:none` override that hid the connector entirely. These were consolidated into a single variable-based rule (see §19.9).

#### 19.2.3 Shared CSS — NS and TP get this fix automatically

`.tp-grid` is the shared grid class for **Diagnostic Procedure**, **Nursing Skill**, and **Therapeutic Procedure**. All three template types automatically inherit the box styling and connector fixes. NS and TP were verified by visual spot-check after DP approval and required no additional changes.
### 19.3 Growth and Development (A5) — APPROVED v8

The most structurally distinct fix in this pass. The canonical G&D template is **8 boxes in 2 groups** with a hierarchical tree connecting the Health Promotion parent to its 4 children.

**Canonical structure:**

- **Top group** (with dark wrapper, label "EXPECTED GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT" as section divider with horizontal lines on either side):
  - 4 boxes in a single row: Physical Development | Cognitive Development | Psychosocial Development | Age-Appropriate Activities
- **Bottom group — NO dark wrapper** in canonical:
  - **Health Promotion** parent box (wide, full-width labeled box with stage-specific content)
  - 4 vertical connector lines descending from the parent box
  - 4 child boxes side-by-side: Immunizations | Health Screening | Nutrition | Injury Prevention

#### 19.3.1 Grid: 2-column → 4-column

The original `.gd-grid > .tpl-group > .tpl-group-body` used `grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr` (2×2 layout). Canonical requires single-row 4-column layout. Updated:

```css
.gd-grid > .tpl-group > .tpl-group-body {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr));
  gap: 12px;
}
@media (max-width: 1100px) {
  .gd-grid > .tpl-group > .tpl-group-body { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); }
}
@media (max-width: 600px) {
  .gd-grid > .tpl-group > .tpl-group-body { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
}
```

Section labels were also restyled as horizontal-line dividers using flex with `::before` and `::after` pseudo-elements rendering a 1px line on each side of the label text.

#### 19.3.2 Health Promotion tree structure

The bottom group required a complete DOM and CSS rewrite. Original structure was identical to the top group (label + 4-box body). Canonical structure is hierarchical:

**New DOM structure** (applied to each of 6 G&D cards — 1 MN Newborn + 5 PD stages):

```html
<div class="tpl-group health-promotion-group">
  <div class="hp-parent">
    <h3>Health Promotion</h3>
    <div class="content">
      <ul>
        <li>Stage-specific anticipatory guidance bullet 1</li>
        <li>Stage-specific anticipatory guidance bullet 2</li>
        ...
      </ul>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="hp-connectors" aria-hidden="true">
    <span></span><span></span><span></span><span></span>
  </div>
  <div class="tpl-group-body">
    <div class="tp-box"><h3>Immunizations</h3>...</div>
    <div class="tp-box"><h3>Health Screening</h3>...</div>
    <div class="tp-box"><h3>Nutrition</h3>...</div>
    <div class="tp-box"><h3>Injury Prevention</h3>...</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

**Supporting CSS:**

```css
/* No outer wrapper for the HP group — canonical has the dark wrapper only on Expected G&D */
.gd-grid > .tpl-group.health-promotion-group {
  background: transparent !important;
  border: 0 !important;
  border-radius: 0 !important;
  padding: 0 !important;
  display: flex !important;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 0;
}
/* Parent box has the same darker h3 strip + lighter content pattern as other tp-boxes */
.gd-grid > .tpl-group.health-promotion-group > .hp-parent {

  border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: 14px;
  overflow: hidden;
}
.gd-grid > .tpl-group.health-promotion-group > .hp-parent > h3 {
  background: var(--surface2);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
  /* DM Serif Display 400 15px */
}
/* Connector strip aligned with the 4 child columns below */
.gd-grid > .tpl-group.health-promotion-group {
  --hp-connector-height: 20px;
  --hp-connector-width: 3px;
}
.gd-grid > .tpl-group.health-promotion-group > .hp-connectors {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr));
  gap: 12px;
  height: var(--hp-connector-height);
}
.gd-grid > .tpl-group.health-promotion-group > .hp-connectors > span {
  display: block;
  width: var(--hp-connector-width);
  height: var(--hp-connector-height);
  background: var(--text3);
  justify-self: center;
  border-radius: 1px;
}
```

#### 19.3.3 Stage-specific Health Promotion content

The HP parent box was authored with anticipatory guidance overview content for each developmental stage. Each stage's content is a 6-7 bullet summary covering screening, anticipatory guidance priorities, key vaccines, safety, and developmentally-appropriate considerations. Stages covered:

- **Newborn (MN)** — newborn screening, feeding establishment, safe sleep, bonding, warning signs
- **Infant (PD)** — well-child schedule (1-12mo), trust-building, safe sleep, childproofing, vaccinations
- **Toddler (PD)** — autonomy, toilet training, safety priority, physiologic anorexia, discipline, screen time
- **Preschool (PD)** — kindergarten readiness, 4-6yr immunization boosters, vision/hearing, safety teaching, magical thinking
- **School-age (PD)** — school adjustment, tween vaccines (11-12yr), sports safety, mental health screening
- **Adolescent (PD)** — confidentiality, sexual health, mental health, substance use, motor vehicle, HPV completion

The injection was done via Python regex matching `<dt>Developmental Stage</dt><dd><span class="meta-value">STAGE</span>...` and replacing the empty `<div class="hp-parent"><h3>Health Promotion</h3></div>` with the stage-appropriate populated version.

#### 19.3.4 Wrapper styling decision

Initially the HP group was given the same dark wrapper as Expected G&D for consistency. Mark clarified that canonical has the wrapper **only on the top (Expected G&D) group**, not on Health Promotion. Removed via `!important` override of inherited `.tpl-group` styles.
### 19.4 Medication (A7) — APPROVED v9

The highest-volume template type (14 MN + 13 PD + 41 Pharm = **68 medication cards**) and the one requiring the most structural surgery. Multiple iterations addressed: missing fields, content-area positioning, column proportions, independent column flow, vertical connector geometry, and a CSS specificity conflict.

**Canonical structure:**

- Header banner: "ACTIVE LEARNING TEMPLATE: Medication" (gray bar)
- Meta header: STUDENT NAME (row 1), MEDICATION + REVIEW MODULE CHAPTER (row 2 side-by-side), **CATEGORY CLASS** (row 3)
- **PURPOSE OF MEDICATION** label + dark wrapper containing 2 boxes: Expected Pharmacological Action | Therapeutic Use
- Two-column body (no outer wrapper):
  - **Left column** (wider, 4 boxes): Complications · Contraindications/Precautions · Interactions · Evaluation of Medication Effectiveness
  - **Right column** (narrower, 3 boxes): Medication Administration · Nursing Interventions · Client Education
- **Vertical connector** between Nursing Interventions and Client Education in the right column
- Bottoms of both columns align (last box in the shorter column expands to fill)

#### 19.4.1 Add CATEGORY CLASS field

PD already had Category Class in its DOM (via `<dt>Category Class</dt><dd>...`). MN and Pharm were missing it. The field renders alongside Medication and Review Module Chapter in the meta header `<dl>`.

#### 19.4.2 Move "Evaluation of Medication Effectiveness" into the left column

In the initial layout, this box was placed full-width at the bottom of the medication card, **outside** the body grid. Canonical has it as the 4th box in the left column.

Move pattern (regex):

```python
pattern = re.compile(
    r'(</div>)\s*'  # closes med-body
    r'(<div class="tp-box[^"]*>\s*<h3>Evaluation of Medication Effectiveness</h3>.*?</div>)\s*'
    r'(</div>)',     # closes med-grid
    re.DOTALL
)
# Rearrange so the Evaluation box goes INSIDE med-body (before its closing </div>)
```

Applied to 12 MN cards and 41 Pharm cards. PD's structure differed (see §19.4.4).

#### 19.4.3 Column proportions — left wider than right

Original CSS used equal columns (`1fr 1fr`). Canonical's left column is visibly wider. Updated to:

```css
.med-body {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1.4fr 1fr;  /* later changed — see §19.4.5 */
}
```

#### 19.4.4 PD-specific restructure: grouped → alternating order

PD's medication cards used a completely different DOM structure: `<div class="tpl-group med-body">` (with extra `tpl-group` class causing an unwanted dark wrapper) and boxes in **grouped order** (all left-column boxes first, then all right-column boxes), with a separate `<div class="tpl-group evaluation">` wrapper for the Evaluation box.

In a 2-column row-flow grid, this grouped order would render as:

```
Row 1: Complications        | Contraindications/Precautions
Row 2: Interactions         | Medication Administration
Row 3: Nursing Interventions | Client Education
```

Which is **wrong** vs. canonical. To get the canonical layout, boxes must alternate left/right:

```
Row 1: Complications                  | Medication Administration
Row 2: Contraindications/Precautions  | Nursing Interventions
Row 3: Interactions                   | Client Education
Row 4: Evaluation                     | (empty)
```

A depth-aware Python script (`Restructurer` class) processed each PD medication card:

1. Located the `<div class="tpl-group med-body">` block and its closing `</div>` via balanced-div parsing.
2. Located the adjacent `<div class="tpl-group evaluation">` wrapper.
3. Extracted every `<div class="tp-box">` with its full nested content (including the `<div class="content">` body), keyed by its `<h3>` heading text.
4. Rebuilt the body in canonical alternating order, dropping the `tpl-group` class from `med-body` and discarding the standalone `evaluation` wrapper.
5. Added the `med-ni` and `med-ce` classes to Nursing Interventions and Client Education boxes (required for the connector — see §19.4.7).

After this pass, all 13 PD cards had the same DOM structure as MN/Pharm.

#### 19.4.5 Independent column flow — switch from CSS grid to flexbox columns

Even with the alternating order, the 2-column grid forced row alignment between left and right boxes. Canonical boxes have **independent heights** in each column — Client Education sits visibly lower than its left neighbor in many canonical examples because each column's boxes flow to their content-appropriate heights.

**Final structure** — wrap left and right boxes in dedicated column containers:

```html
<div class="med-body">
  <div class="med-col-left">
    <div class="tp-box">Complications</div>
    <div class="tp-box">Contraindications/Precautions</div>
    <div class="tp-box">Interactions</div>
    <div class="tp-box">Evaluation of Medication Effectiveness</div>
  </div>
  <div class="med-col-right">
    <div class="tp-box">Medication Administration</div>
    <div class="tp-box med-ni">Nursing Interventions</div>
    <div class="tp-box med-ce">Client Education</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

**Supporting CSS** (variable-based, see §19.4.8):

```css
.med-body {
  --med-gap: 14px;
  --connector-overlap: 2px;
  display: flex;
  gap: var(--med-gap);
  position: relative;
}
.med-body > .med-col-left  { flex: 1.4; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--med-gap); }
.med-body > .med-col-right { flex: 1;   display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--med-gap); }

/* Box styling — descendant selector required since boxes are nested inside column wrappers */
.med-body .tp-box {
  background: var(--surface);
  border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: 14px;
  padding: 0 !important;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  min-height: 120px;
}
.med-body .tp-box > h3 {
  background: var(--surface2);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-top-left-radius: 13px;
  border-top-right-radius: 13px;
  /* DM Serif Display 400 15px */
}
.med-body .tp-box > .content { padding: 14px 16px 16px; flex: 1; }

/* Column bottoms align: last box in each column stretches to fill remaining space */
.med-body > .med-col-left  > .tp-box:last-child,
.med-body > .med-col-right > .tp-box:last-child { flex-grow: 1; }

@media (max-width: 680px) {
  .med-body { flex-direction: column; }
}
```

**Restructure applied to all 68 medication cards** via Python script that:
- Located each `<div class="med-body">...</div>` using depth-aware div parsing
- Extracted boxes by heading
- Rebuilt with the column-wrapper structure
- Skipped already-restructured cards (sentinel attribute) to allow idempotent re-runs

#### 19.4.6 Box styling broke after the restructure

After wrapping boxes in `.med-col-left` / `.med-col-right`, the existing CSS selectors targeting `.med-body > .tp-box` (direct-child combinator) stopped matching. Boxes lost their borders, header strips, and backgrounds — rendering as plain text headings with content.

**Fix:** Change selectors from `>` (direct child) to descendant: `.med-body .tp-box`. This catches boxes wherever they're nested under `.med-body`, including inside the column wrappers.

#### 19.4.7 Connector — Nursing Interventions → Client Education

A small vertical line links Nursing Interventions (right column, middle) to Client Education (right column, below it). After the restructure, the original selector `.med-body > .med-ni::after` no longer matched (NI was inside `.med-col-right`, not directly inside `.med-body`).

**The trap that delayed this for several iterations:**

An OLD conflicting CSS rule remained in the file from an earlier session:

```css
.med-body > .tp-box.med-ni::after {  /* 4 classes — high specificity */
  bottom: -9px;
  height: 18px;
  /* ... */
}
```

This rule had **higher specificity** than my newer `.med-body .med-ni::after` (3 classes), so the cascade favored it — locking the connector's geometry to the wrong values regardless of how I edited the new rule.

**Diagnosis pattern:** When a CSS edit appears to have no effect, search the file for **all** rules matching the same selector pattern (`.med-ni::after`, `.complications::after`, etc.) and look for higher-specificity duplicates. The audit revealed 5 different `.med-ni::after` rules. Removed the obsolete higher-specificity rule and the cascade resolved to the intended rule.

#### 19.4.8 Robust variable-based connector geometry

The connector is now driven entirely by CSS variables on `.med-body`:

```css
.med-body {
  --med-gap: 14px;          /* row/column gap — single source of truth */
  --connector-overlap: 2px; /* how far the line penetrates each adjacent box */
}
.med-body .med-ni { position: relative; }
.med-body .med-ni::after {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  left: 50%;
  transform: translateX(-50%);
  bottom: calc(-1 * var(--med-gap) - var(--connector-overlap));
  width: 3px;
  height: calc(var(--med-gap) + 2 * var(--connector-overlap));
  background: var(--text3);
  border-radius: 1px;
  z-index: 5;
}
```

**Why this is robust:**

- Box height changes → connector anchors to NI's bottom edge, so it follows automatically.
- Box width changes → `left: 50% + translateX(-50%)` always centers horizontally.
- Gap value changes → flip `--med-gap` from `14px` to any other value; column gap AND connector geometry update together.
- Connector overlap into boxes changes → flip `--connector-overlap` from `2px` to whatever you want.

**The non-dynamic part (caveats):**

- The `gap` declaration on `.med-col-left` / `.med-col-right` must keep referencing `var(--med-gap)`. If anyone later hardcodes `gap: 20px`, the actual gap and the connector's calculated span would diverge. The variable is the contract.
- If extra spacing is added between NI and CE that isn't from the flex `gap` (e.g., a margin-top on CE), the variable wouldn't account for that.

### 19.9 Connector design pattern — line-under-box approach (definitive)

Three template families have connector lines:

| Family | Templates | Connector | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.tp-grid` | Diagnostic Procedure · Nursing Skill · Therapeutic Procedure | Potential Complications ↔ Nursing Interventions | Horizontal |
| `.med-body` | Medication | Nursing Interventions ↓ Client Education | Vertical |
| `.health-promotion-group` | Growth & Development | HP parent ↓ 4 child boxes | 4 parallel verticals |

All three use the same architecture: **the line is generously oversized (extending well into both adjacent boxes), placed BEHIND the boxes via `z-index: -1`, and the boxes' opaque backgrounds visually clip it — only the gap portion is visible.** A self-contained stacking context (`isolation: isolate` on the parent) bounds the negative z-index so it doesn't escape.

#### 19.9.1 The core principle — why "line under the box"

Earlier iterations tried to terminate the line exactly at the box edges using small overlap values (0px, 1px, 2px). All failed due to subpixel rendering — at zoom levels and on different displays, the line ends could leave hairline gaps or visibly cross into the box content.

The fix: **stop trying to terminate the line precisely.** Extend it generously into both adjacent boxes (10px overlap on each side), place it behind the boxes with `z-index: -1`, and let the opaque box backgrounds (`var(--surface)`) visually clip it. The portions inside the boxes are invisible because they're covered. Only the portion in the gap shows.

Required pieces:

1. **The connector** at `z-index: -1` with width/height extended `gap + 2*overlap` so it overlaps `overlap` pixels into each adjacent box
2. **A stacking context** on the parent via `isolation: isolate` (so `z-index: -1` is bounded — doesn't go behind the whole page)
3. **Opaque box backgrounds** (already present via `.tp-box { background: var(--surface); }`)

#### 19.9.2 Pattern A — Horizontal connector across a grid gap (`.tp-grid`)

Used for DP / NS / TP. The two boxes sit in adjacent grid cells. The connector pseudo-element extends across the gap, overlapping into both boxes.

```css
.tp-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
  grid-template-areas:
    "description description"
    "indications considerations"
    "outcomes considerations"
    "complications nursing-interventions";
  gap: var(--tp-gap);
  position: relative;
  isolation: isolate;          /* bounds z-index: -1 to this container */
  --tp-gap: 14px;              /* must match grid gap value */
  --tp-connector-overlap: 10px; /* line extends this far into each box */
}
.tp-grid > .complications,
.tp-grid > .nursing-interventions { position: relative; }
.tp-grid > .complications::after {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  top: 50%;
  right: calc(-1 * (var(--tp-gap) + var(--tp-connector-overlap)));
  transform: translateY(-50%);
  width: calc(var(--tp-gap) + 2 * var(--tp-connector-overlap));  /* 14 + 20 = 34px */
  height: 3px;
  background: var(--text3);
  border-radius: 1px;
  z-index: -1;                 /* behind the boxes; only gap portion shows */
}
@media (max-width: 680px) { .tp-grid > .complications::after { display: none; } }
```

Math: line spans 34px total — 10px under Complications (hidden by its background), 14px in the gap (visible), 10px under Nursing Interventions (hidden by its background).

#### 19.9.3 Pattern B — Vertical connector across a flex-column gap (`.med-body`)

Used for Medication. Same approach as Pattern A but vertical.

```css
.med-body {
  display: flex;
  gap: var(--med-gap);
  position: relative;
  isolation: isolate;
  --med-gap: 14px;
  --connector-overlap: 10px;
}
.med-col-right { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--med-gap); }

.med-body .med-ni { position: relative; }
.med-body .med-ni::after {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  left: 50%;
  transform: translateX(-50%);
  bottom: calc(-1 * var(--med-gap) - var(--connector-overlap));
  width: 3px;
  height: calc(var(--med-gap) + 2 * var(--connector-overlap));  /* 34px */
  background: var(--text3);
  border-radius: 1px;
  z-index: -1;
}
```

#### 19.9.4 Pattern C — Multiple parallel connectors in a dedicated strip (`.health-promotion-group`)

Used for Growth & Development. The 4 connectors are explicit DOM elements (`<span>` inside `.hp-connectors`), not pseudo-elements. They sit in a dedicated strip between the parent and child rows. Same trick — extend each span beyond the strip via `height + 20px` and `margin-top: -10px`, with `z-index: -1` so the parent and child boxes cover the overflow.

```css
.gd-grid > .tpl-group.health-promotion-group {
  display: flex !important;
  flex-direction: column;
  isolation: isolate;          /* bounds z-index: -1 */
  --hp-connector-height: 20px;
  --hp-connector-width: 3px;
}
.gd-grid > .tpl-group.health-promotion-group > .hp-connectors {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr));
  gap: 12px;  /* must match the child-row gap below */
  height: var(--hp-connector-height);  /* strip height = 20px */
  pointer-events: none;
}
.gd-grid > .tpl-group.health-promotion-group > .hp-connectors > span {
  display: block;
  width: var(--hp-connector-width);
  /* Extended: 20px strip height + 20px extension = 40px total */
  height: calc(var(--hp-connector-height) + 20px);
  margin-top: -10px;           /* shift up so 10px overlaps parent above */
  background: var(--text3);
  justify-self: center;
  border-radius: 1px;
  position: relative;
  z-index: -1;
}
```

Each span is 40px tall in a 20px strip with `margin-top: -10px` — it visually extends 10px above the strip (into the parent box) and 10px below (into the child boxes row). Both ends are covered by the boxes' opaque backgrounds.

#### 19.9.5 Common rules for all three patterns

| Property | Value | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Color | `var(--text3)` | Darker neutral — visible on both dark and light backgrounds |
| Thickness | 3px | Visible without being heavy |
| Border-radius | 1px | Slight rounding for polish |
| **z-index** | **-1** | Behind boxes so their backgrounds clip the line ends |
| **Overlap** | **10px** | Generous extension; far more than needed; covered by box backgrounds |
| **Parent stacking context** | **`isolation: isolate`** | Bounds the negative z-index to the parent container |
| Mobile | Hidden via media query | When layout collapses to single column, no gap to span |

#### 19.9.6 Why `isolation: isolate` matters

CSS `z-index: -1` does NOT, by default, place an element behind all other content. It places the element behind other elements **within the same stacking context**. Without `isolation: isolate` on the parent, the connector at `z-index: -1` could escape to whatever ancestor creates the next stacking context — which is fine in most cases but unpredictable near other positioned elements.

`isolation: isolate` is the modern, declarative way to create a stacking context. With it on `.tp-grid`, `.med-body`, and `.health-promotion-group`, the connectors' `z-index: -1` is precisely contained: behind in-flow boxes within these containers, but not behind anything outside them.

#### 19.9.7 Why CSS variables matter — the brittleness lesson

The original connectors used hardcoded pixel offsets:

```css
/* Old: brittle */
.med-ni::after { bottom: -9px; height: 18px; }
```

This is bound to a specific gap value. If anyone later changed the column gap, the connector wouldn't span correctly. The variable-based version makes the relationship between gap and connector geometry **explicit and synchronized** — changing the gap value updates everything downstream.

#### 19.9.8 Iteration history (for context — don't implement these)

The current approach was reached after four iterations. Documenting them so the rejected approaches aren't tried again:

| Iteration | Approach | Why it failed |
|---|---|---|
| v1 | 2px overlap, no z-index trick | Line visibly crossed into box content area |
| v2 | 0px overlap (line ends exactly at borders) | Subpixel rendering created hairline gaps |
| v3 | 1px overlap | Still subpixel-fragile depending on zoom |
| **v4 (current)** | **10px overlap + z-index: -1 + isolation: isolate** | **Works robustly — box backgrounds clip the line** |

The first three all attempted pixel-precise termination. The lesson: **don't terminate the line precisely — extend it generously, then hide the overlap.**

### 19.10 Lessons learned — debugging patterns and common pitfalls

These patterns came up repeatedly during the canonical compliance pass and are worth carrying forward to any future template work.

#### 19.10.1 When a CSS edit appears to have no effect: audit ALL rules matching the selector

The medication connector took multiple iterations to track down because an old higher-specificity rule from a previous session remained in the file:

```css
.med-body > .tp-box.med-ni::after { /* 4 classes — wins the cascade */ }
.med-body .med-ni::after { /* 3 classes — never applied */ }
```

**Debug pattern:** When edits to a CSS rule don't visibly change the output, search the entire file for all rules matching the same selector (or pattern). Look for higher-specificity siblings, `!important` overrides, and `display:none` rules. Use:

```python
for m in re.finditer(r'\.med-ni::after\s*\{[^}]*\}', css):
    print(m.group(0))
```

Then either delete the obsolete rules or raise the specificity of the intended rule.

#### 19.10.2 `overflow: hidden` on a box clips its connector pseudo-elements

Connector pseudo-elements (`::after`, `::before`) positioned with negative offsets to extend past the parent box are clipped when the parent has `overflow: hidden`. This applied to the `.tp-grid > .tp-box` rule during the DP fix.

**Workaround:** Don't use `overflow: hidden` on the box. Instead, give the box's header (`h3`) its own rounded top corners via `border-top-left-radius` / `border-top-right-radius`. The header's rectangle will self-clip to the box's rounded shape because its corners are rounded to match. The box bottom stays rounded automatically because the content's background matches the box's background.

#### 19.10.3 Direct-child combinators (`>`) break when DOM structure is wrapped

Pre-existing rule:

```css
.med-body > .tp-box { /* styling */ }
```

After wrapping boxes in column containers (`.med-col-left`, `.med-col-right`), this selector no longer matched — boxes lost all their styling.

**Workaround:** Use the descendant combinator (a space) instead of `>`:

```css
.med-body .tp-box { /* styling, applies regardless of nesting depth */ }
```

This is less precise but more resilient to structural changes. The trade-off is the rule will also apply to any deeper `.tp-box` nested inside other elements — usually fine.

#### 19.10.4 When boxes in two columns need bottom-alignment

For columns that flow independently but should end at the same Y position (medication's "bottoms align" requirement), give the last box in each column `flex-grow: 1`:

```css
.med-body > .med-col-left  > .tp-box:last-child,
.med-body > .med-col-right > .tp-box:last-child { flex-grow: 1; }
```

All other boxes take their natural content-sized height. Only the last box expands to fill remaining space, so both columns end at the same height (the taller column's natural height).

#### 19.10.5 Per-template iteration vs. bulk changes

This pass deliberately fixed one template type at a time, with visual approval between each, rather than speculatively bulk-applying fixes across the 369 cards. Benefits:

- **Catches surprises early.** PD's medication structure was completely different from MN/Pharm; if a bulk fix had assumed the same DOM shape, it would have silently failed on 13 cards.
- **Bounds the blast radius.** Each fix touched a known scope; reverting a fix was a single backup checkpoint away.
- **Builds confidence.** Visual approval after each template ensured no regressions slipped through.

Per-card backups (`/home/claude/pre_<step>_backup/`) were taken before each structural change. Validation via `node --check` ran after every CSS or HTML write.

## PART 20 — PHASE 3: PEDAGOGICAL UNIFICATION & MENTAL HEALTH SUITE

This part documents Phase 3, in which all four review books were brought to a single unified pedagogical format and the Mental Health (MH) subject was completed and wired into the suite. By the end of Phase 3 the suite is **content-complete across all four ATI review modules** (Maternal Newborn, Nursing Care of Children, Pharmacology, Mental Health) and is a genuine digital replacement for the physical books' review questions.

### 20.0 Goals & scope

Phase 3's thesis: every chapter in every book should carry the same study scaffold so the experience is identical regardless of subject. The unified per-chapter format is:

1. **Chapter banner** — unit/name/number metadata + an italic chapter title + a one-line lede.
2. **TL;DR brief-card** — a one-glance summary paragraph plus a 2-cell `brief-grid` of sub-cards.
3. **Active Learning Scenario (ALS)** — the chapter's ATI ALS rendered in the canonical template style.
4. **Application Exercises** — the chapter's ATI Application Exercises, each with lettered options, a collapsible answer + per-option rationale, and an NCLEX® Connection tag.

Concept "pills" (`condition-block` articles) are retained where a book already had them (e.g., MH Unit 1) but were **not** retrofitted into stub chapters during Phase 3 — that was deferred in favor of getting exercises onto every chapter first (the "exercises-first pass").

### 20.1 The unified chapter HTML skeleton

Every Phase 3 chapter section follows this exact shape (MH shown; other books differ only in unit/chapter labels and theme):

```html
<section class="chapter" id="chN">
  <div class="chapter-banner">
    <div class="chapter-meta">Unit X · UNIT NAME · Chapter N</div>
    <h2 class="chapter-name"><em>TITLE</em></h2>
    <p class="chapter-lede">One-line orientation to the chapter.</p>
  </div>

  <section id="chN-tldr" class="brief-card">
    <h2>TL;DR · One-glance summary</h2>
    <p class="tldr"><strong>…</strong> compact high-yield summary …</p>
    <div class="brief-grid">
      <div><h3>Sub-card A</h3><ul><li>…</li></ul></div>
      <div><h3>Sub-card B</h3><ul><li>…</li></ul></div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section id="chN-als" class="content-section">
    <h2>Active Learning Scenario</h2>
    <p class="section-lead">Case-based reasoning using the ATI Active Learning Template: <em>TYPE</em>.</p>
    <article class="als-card">
      <header class="als-head">
        <h3>Scenario title</h3>
        <span class="als-tag">TYPE · subtitle</span>
      </header>
      <div class="als-stem"><p>Scenario stem …</p></div>
      <div class="als-grid">
        <div class="als-card-section"><h4>Section heading</h4><p>…</p></div>
        <!-- 2–3 als-card-section blocks matching the template's required fields -->
      </div>
    </article>
  </section>

  <section id="chN-exercises" class="content-section">
    <h2>Application Exercises</h2>
    <p class="section-lead">Practice questions reflecting how this content appears on the NCLEX-RN. Rationales source the ATI Application Exercises Key.</p>

    <div class="exercise" data-difficulty="medium|hard">
      <div class="exercise-stem">
        <h3>Exercise N.M — Subtitle</h3>
        <p>Stem … <strong>(Select all that apply.)</strong></p>  <!-- SATA stems end with this exact phrase -->
        <ol class="exercise-options" type="A"><li>…</li></ol>
      </div>
      <details class="exercise-rationale">
        <summary>Show answer &amp; rationale</summary>
        <p><strong>Answer: X</strong></p>  <!-- or "Answer: B, D" for SATA; "Answer: C, A, B, E, D" for ordering -->
        <ul><li><strong>A. Correct/Incorrect</strong> — …</li></ul>
        <p class="nclex-tag">NCLEX® Connection: Category — Subcategory</p>
      </details>
    </div>
    <!-- one .exercise per question -->
  </section>
</section>
```

Difficulty heuristic: single-answer recall/teaching items are `medium`; SATA, priority/"first action", ordering, and multi-step reasoning items are `hard`.

### 20.2 PDF source parsing & column detection

The ATI review-module PDFs are two-column. Extraction and parsing rules that proved reliable:

- **Extract with layout preserved:** `pdftotext -layout source.pdf full_layout.txt`. Keep a plain (`pdftotext source.pdf plain.txt`) fallback.
- **Read in Python with `errors='replace'`.** The layout text contains invalid UTF-8 bytes; `bash cut` chokes on them, but `open(..., encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')` then slicing by character column works.
- **Column detection:** a question column is identified when a line matches `re.match(r'\s+\d+\. A nurse', line[:70])`. If the questions are in the **left** column, slice characters `0–57` (or `0–70`); otherwise the questions are in the **right** column, slice `58–140` (or `58–148`).
- **The ALS sits in the opposite column from the questions** on a given page, and the Application Exercises Key is usually on the facing/next column or page.
- **Verify the chapter** by the running page footer `CHAPTER N Title`.
- **Layout variants:** some chapters are "compact" (questions left + key right on one marker line); some split Q1–3 left and Q4–5 right; some have the ALS on the questions page, others a page earlier.
- **Exercise counts vary:** most chapters have 5; some have 4 (e.g., MH Ch 33), 2 (MH Ch 29 Crisis Management), or 6 (Pharm Ch 48). **Never assume 5** — read the key to confirm the true count.
- **MH `-layout` extraction is flaky:** it intermittently yields a 73-line truncated file; simply **re-running** the same command succeeds. Always sanity-check the extracted line count (MH full layout ≈ 15,020 lines) before parsing.

### 20.3 The injection + verify-before-write method

New chapter content was authored into addon files with sentinel markers, then injected into the live book with a hard verify gate (the shared CORE is ⭐ §23.4). This pattern ran for every batch:

```python
def chap_span(html, n):
    start = html.find(f'<section class="chapter" id="ch{n}">')
    if start == -1: return None
    nxt = html.find('<section class="chapter" id="ch', start+10)
    return (start, nxt if nxt != -1 else html.find('</main>', start))
```

Rules:

- **Process chapters in REVERSE order** within a batch, so earlier injections don't shift the byte offsets of later ones.
- **Guard on the stub sentinel.** Only replace a chapter span if the placeholder text `"Chapter content will be added in a later phase"` is still present — this makes re-runs idempotent and prevents clobbering already-built chapters.
- **Verify-before-write gate** (mandatory): recount after the in-memory edit and only write to disk if **all** hold:
  - exercise delta == expected for the batch (e.g., +20, or +17 when a chapter has 2),
  - ALS delta == number of chapters in the batch,
  - concept-pill count unchanged,
  - JS errors == 0 (extract each non-src `<script>` block to a temp file and run `node --check`).
- Addons live at `/home/claude/mh_chNN-NN_addon.html` with `<!-- ==CHN== -->…<!-- ==/CHN== -->` markers per chapter.

### 20.4 Pharmacology — Phase C completion (v3.3.0)

Pharm's final enrichment batch covered Ch 46–49 (UTIs; Mycobacterial/Fungal/Parasitic; Viral/HIV/AIDS [6 exercises]; Complementary/Alternative). Final Pharm state: **251 Application Exercises** (166 medium / 87 hard) across all 49 chapters, 50 ALS, 108 concept pills, JS valid, ~1.42 MB. Version bumped 3.2.0 → **3.3.0**.

An exercises-first pass built real TL;DR + ALS + Application Exercises for all 27 stubs across seven batches:

- Batch 2 — Ch 11–14 (Unit 3): 20 ex + 4 ALS

**Final MH state:** 161 Application Exercises (91 medium / 71 hard) across all 33 chapters, **33 ALS** (one per chapter), 128 concept pills (Unit 1 only), 0 stub placeholders, JS valid, ~710 KB. Version bumped 3.1.1 → **3.2.0**.

**MH unit structure (6 units / 33 chapters):**

### 20.6 Sensitive-content handling (non-negotiable)
**→ See ⭐ §26.3 (canonical sensitive-content framework)** for the per-topic rules (eating-disorder qualitative-only, suicide/means omission, violence + sexual-assault framing). This Phase-3 section first established those guardrails; they are now codified in §26.3.

**Unique rule preserved here — ATI-key faithfulness under sensitive content:** answers follow the ATI Application Exercises Key even where clinically debatable (e.g., Ch 30 Q5 frames a no-suicide contract as risk-reducing, per ATI). Rationales remain accurate and note the ATI position where relevant. Never fabricate exercises. Sensitive-content guardrails (§26.3) and ATI-key faithfulness are applied together.
### 20.7 MH suite hub build (clone + theme swap)

The MH hub (`Elevated ATI MH Hub.html`, v3.2.0) was built by cloning the Pharm hub to inherit the identical CSS/design, then:

- **Theme swap (lime):** `--accent` `#ea580c → #65a30d`; `--accent2` `#c2410c → #4d7c0f`; `--accent-soft` `rgba(234,88,12,…) → rgba(101,163,13,…)`; and the easily-missed **`<meta name="theme-color">`** in the head (this was the lone orange leftover after the variable swap — always grep for `#ea580c`/`#c2410c` after theming).
- **Body tailored to MH's single tool.** MH has only a Book (no Templates, no Flashcards), so the Templates card, Flashcards card, flashcard review-queue, and template-types section were removed rather than carried over as broken/empty UI. They appear under "Planned additions" instead.
- **Focused, self-contained JS** (not the Pharm flashcard/template logic): theme toggle, book + per-unit reading progress from `nur2460_atimh_progress`, a "Continue reading" pickup from `nur2460_last_chapter` (guarded by `/^ch([1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[0-3])$/`), and an export/import/reset storage panel scoped to `SYNC_KEYS = ['nur2460_atimh_progress','nur2460_atimh_bookmarks','nur2460_nclex_done','nur2460_theme']`.
- **Six-unit breakdown** with `data-unit`/`data-unit-bar`/`data-unit-text` cards mirroring the Pharm units-grid.

Stats row reflects what MH actually has: **33 Chapters · 6 Units · 161 Application Exercises · 33 Active Learning Scenarios**.

### 20.8 Index wiring (4th subject)

`index.html` (bumped to v3.2.0) gained Mental Health as a fourth subject:

- Added `--mh-color:#65a30d;` in **both** the dark `:root` and the light-theme variable blocks.
- Added the rule `[data-subject="mh"]{ --card-color:var(--mh-color) }` after the pharm rule.
- Added a 4th `.subject-card` (`data-subject="mh"`, mark `MH`, course `ATI · Mental Health`, name `Mental Health`) after the Pharmacology card, linking to `Elevated%20ATI%20MH%20Hub.html`.
- **Adapted the 3-stat block** to MH's reality: Chapters 33 / Exercises 161 / Scenarios 33 (instead of the Templates/Cards used by the other subjects, which MH doesn't have).

### 20.9 MH Book unit-bar config fix

The MH Book's in-page accordion markup already contained all six unit sections (`unit1acc`–`unit6acc`, each with `unitNcount`/`unitNbar`/`unitNbarpartial` elements) and all 33 chapter checkboxes (`data-toggle-check="chN"`). However, the JS `unitChapters` config was a stale four-entry scaffold (unit1=ch1–10, unit2=ch11–16, unit3=ch17–22, unit4=ch23–27) — so units 5–6 never updated and units 1–4 mis-counted. Fix = replace the config to match the real accordion ranges:

```javascript
var unitChapters = {
  unit1acc: ['ch1','ch2','ch3','ch4','ch5','ch6'],
  unit2acc: ['ch7','ch8','ch9','ch10'],
  unit3acc: ['ch11','ch12','ch13','ch14','ch15','ch16','ch17','ch18','ch19','ch20'],
  unit4acc: ['ch21','ch22','ch23','ch24','ch25','ch26'],
  unit5acc: ['ch27','ch28'],
  unit6acc: ['ch29','ch30','ch31','ch32','ch33']
};
```

**Lesson:** when porting/scaffolding a book, the unit→chapter map in the JS and the unit→chapter grouping in the markup are two independent sources of truth that must be reconciled. Always verify the config against the actual accordion contents (parse `data-toggle-check` IDs between consecutive `unitNacc` anchors), not against assumptions.

### 20.10 GitHub deployment workflow

Repo: `github.com/SleepyIus/Elevated-ATI-Books`; Pages: `sleepyius.github.io/Elevated-ATI-Books/`. The sandbox has **no stored GitHub token** and resets between sessions, and the unauthenticated API returns 403 — so deployment is a **manual upload by the user**: GitHub web → *Add file → Upload files* → drag the changed files → commit; Pages auto-redeploys.

- **Repo filenames use spaces** (e.g., `Elevated ATI MH Book.html`); links in `index.html` use the `%20`-encoded form. Upload with the **exact spaced names** so files overwrite rather than duplicate.
- **The Build Guide is INTERNAL ONLY — never upload it to GitHub.**

Phase 3 close-out upload was four files: `Elevated ATI Pharm Book.html` (v3.3.0), `Elevated ATI MH Book.html` (v3.2.0), the new `Elevated ATI MH Hub.html` (v3.2.0), and `index.html` (v3.2.0).

### 20.11 Lessons learned

- **Verify-before-write gates catch real regressions.** Counting exercise/ALS/pill deltas and running `node --check` before every disk write prevented silent corruption across dozens of injections.
- **Reverse-order injection** is the simplest way to keep byte offsets valid within a multi-chapter batch.
- **Don't trust audit regexes blindly.** An early MH audit reported "10 old als-card divs" to fix; these were false positives where the regex matched `als-card-section`. Always inspect a match before acting on a count.
- **Read the answer key to learn the true exercise count per chapter** — 2, 4, 5, and 6 all occur. Hard-coding 5 would have desynced the verify gate.
- **After any theme swap, grep for the old palette** — the `<meta name="theme-color">` tag and any hard-coded (non-variable) color are the usual stragglers.
- **Clone, then subtract.** Building the MH hub by cloning a complete hub and removing the tools MH lacks produced a visually consistent result faster and more safely than building from scratch — but the removed tools' JS and DOM references must be removed together to avoid dangling element lookups.
- **Sensitive content is written, not avoided** — fully and accurately, but assessment-/safety-/survivor-first, with no method, means, or facilitation detail.

## PART 21 — HIGHLIGHTS + NOTES FEATURE (LIFESPAN PORT)

This part documents adding the **Highlights + Notes** annotation feature to all four ATI book files (MN, PD, Pharm, MH) by porting the proven implementation from the user's separate **Lifespan** book (`lifespan-book.html`). The feature lets the reader select text in a chapter, highlight it in one of four colors, attach a rich-text note, and review/export all highlights from a floating panel.

### 21.0 Why port instead of build from scratch

An initial from-scratch implementation was written and **failed silently** in the user's browser. The root cause (see 21.1) was an architectural assumption. Because the user already had a working, battle-tested version in the Lifespan tool, the correct move was to lift that exact module and adapt only the per-book bits. Lesson: when the user has a proven implementation of a feature in a sibling tool, port it — don't reinvent it.

### 21.1 THE GOTCHA — chapters render in a modal, not the page body

**This is the most important thing to know about the ATI book architecture for any feature that touches chapter text.**

The ATI books do **not** display chapters in a long scrolling page. Instead:

- All chapter `<section class="chapter" id="chN">` blocks live inside a **hidden pool**: `<div class="chapter-pool" id="chapterPool">`.
- A sidebar item (`.sidebar-item[data-section="chN"]`) triggers `window.openChapter(chapterId, initialTabId)`, which **clones the chapter out of the pool into a reading modal**: `<div class="modal-body" id="modalBody">`, building a tab per `:scope > section[id]` (TL;DR / ALS / Exercises) in `<nav class="modal-tabs" id="modalTabs">` (tabs carry `data-tab-for`).
- **The text the user actually reads and selects is inside `#modalBody`** — not in `.main-content` (which is the landing/overview area).

The from-scratch attempt anchored its selection listener and MutationObserver to `.main-content`. Selecting text inside the reading modal therefore triggered nothing, and no highlight UI ever appeared — the module was watching an element the reader never interacts with. **Any annotation/selection feature must target `#modalBody` as its live root and `#chapterPool` as the source-of-truth for chapter metadata.**

Conveniently, the Lifespan book uses the identical architecture (`#modalBody`, `#chapterPool`, `openChapter`, `#modalTabs`, `.sidebar-item[data-section]`, `data-tab-for`), so its module references map 1:1 onto the ATI books with no DOM-integration changes.

### 21.2 Feature components (injected as one fragment before `</body>`)

The fragment is `<style id="lifespan-annotate-style">` + a block of UI `<div>`s + one `<script>` IIFE. UI pieces (all tagged `data-lifespan-ui="1"` so the text-walker skips them):

- **`#lsAnnToolbar`** — selection toolbar: four `.ls-swatch` color buttons (yellow/green/pink/blue) + a `📝 Note` button. Appears on `mouseup` over a non-collapsed selection inside `#modalBody`.
- **`#lsAnnPopover`** — per-highlight editor: draggable header (`#lsPopHeader`, mouse + touch), color swatches, a B/I/U format bar, and a `contenteditable` note field (`#lsNoteEdit`) with Save/Delete.
- **`#lsAnnFab`** — an always-visible floating **🖍 Notes** button (bottom-right) with a live count. This is the discoverability anchor; the from-scratch version lacked it.
- **`#lsAnnOverlay` / `#lsAnnPanel`** — modal listing every highlight grouped by chapter, each with “Go to”, “✎ Note”, and “Delete”, plus a **Copy all** markdown export.

CSS uses `var(--accent, …)` etc., so the FAB and accents **inherit each book's theme color automatically** (amber/sky/orange/lime) — no per-book CSS edits needed. Z-indexes are 235 (FAB) / 240 (toolbar) / 245 (popover) / 250 (overlay); the ATI reading modal (`.modal-overlay`) is z-index **100**, so all annotation UI correctly layers above it.

### 21.3 Storage model — per-book keys + tombstone merge

Two localStorage keys per book:

- `KEY` = `nur2460_ati<subj>_highlights` — JSON **array** of highlight objects.
- `TOMB_KEY` = `nur2460_ati<subj>_highlights_tomb` — JSON **map** `{id: deletedAtTimestamp}`.

Highlight object shape:

```js
{ id, scopeId, chapterId, text, prefix, suffix, gStart, color, note, created, edited }
```

`save()` runs a **tombstone-merge**: union the current and incoming arrays by `id` (newer `edited||created` wins), then drop any id whose tombstone timestamp ≥ the item's last touch. This prevents a deleted highlight from resurrecting when another tab writes a stale copy. A `storage` event listener re-applies and refreshes the FAB/panel when another tab changes the keys.

### 21.4 Re-anchoring (survives chapter close/reopen)

- **`collectTextMap(scope)`** walks `#modalBody`'s (or a section's) text nodes via a TreeWalker, skipping any node under a `[data-lifespan-ui]` element, building `{text, segs:[{node,start,end}]}`.
- **`pointOffset` / `findOffsets`** convert between DOM Range boundaries and absolute offsets in that concatenated text. `findOffsets` tries, in order: the saved `gStart` (if the slice still matches), then `prefix+text+suffix` exact match, then the nearest plain `text` occurrence to `gStart`.
- **`wrapRange`** splits the global `[start,end)` across the intersecting text-node pieces and wraps each piece with `r.surroundContents(<mark class="lifespan-hl" data-hl-id data-hl-color [data-hl-note]>)` — handles highlights spanning inline elements (`<strong>`, `<em>`, links).
- **`reapply()`** unwraps existing marks in `#modalBody`, groups stored highlights by `scopeId`, and re-wraps within each present scope. It is wrapped in `_applying`/observer-disconnect to avoid feedback loops.
- A **MutationObserver on `#modalBody`** (debounced ~60 ms) calls `reapply()` whenever `openChapter` swaps in new content — so highlights reappear automatically each time a chapter/tab is opened.

### 21.5 Porting checklist (per book)

1. Confirm the modal architecture is present: `#modalBody`, `#chapterPool`, `#modalTabs`, `openChapter`, `.sidebar-item[data-section]`, `data-tab-for`. (All four ATI books pass — they share one template.)
2. Confirm `.modal-overlay` z-index < 235 (all are 100).
3. Inject the fragment immediately before the final `</body>`.
4. Change only three things in the fragment: `var KEY`, `var TOMB_KEY` (→ `KEY + '_tomb'`), and the export header title.
5. Verify after injection: exercise/ALS counts unchanged, `node --check` on every script block = 0 errors, each `id="lsAnn…"` appears exactly once (no collision), and `KEY`/`TOMB_KEY` are the intended per-book values.

### 21.6 Per-book storage keys (final)

| Book | KEY | TOMB_KEY |
|---|---|---|
| MN | `nur2460_atimn_highlights` | `nur2460_atimn_highlights_tomb` |
| PD | `nur2460_atipd_highlights` | `nur2460_atipd_highlights_tomb` |
| Pharm | `nur2460_atipharm_highlights` | `nur2460_atipharm_highlights_tomb` |
| MH | `nur2460_atimh_highlights` | `nur2460_atimh_highlights_tomb` |

Keys are fully isolated, so highlights never bleed between subjects.

### 21.7 Coordinated version bump

With the feature on all four books, the suite was bumped to a clean **v3.3.0 · 2026-05-24** across MN, PD, Pharm, and MH (HTML comment + visible badge), with each Status line noting “Highlights + Notes feature added (Lifespan port).” Pharm was already v3.3.0 from its content completion and only had its status updated. The hub and index files remain at v3.2.0 (unaffected by this feature).

## PART 22 — MENTAL HEALTH Ch 7-33 "THOROUGH ENRICHMENT" (CONCEPT PILLS)

### 22.1 Goal & context
The MH book originally carried concept pills only in the foundations chapters (Ch 1-6, 128 pills); Ch 7-33 were exercises-first with a TL;DR and ALS but no concept-pill content sections. The goal was to bring every remaining chapter to **Ch 1-6 depth** so the book is a complete digital replacement for the physical ATI module, not merely a question bank.

An audit first clarified scope. Per-book pill models differ widely (MN ≈ 587 condition-blocks of genuine sub-section content; PD 0; Pharm ≈ 108 across ~10 ch; MH originally 128, Ch 1-6 only). Title-duplicate "redundancy" was a false-positive concern (generic reused headings like "Risk factors" are not redundant content). The real lever was **coverage**, so the pilot was MH Ch 7-33. "Exhaustive" coverage was explicitly rejected (bloat + copyright); the working definition was **"thorough" = match Ch 1-6 depth**, paraphrased as study summaries (never verbatim).

### 22.2 Target format (the pill anatomy)
Ch 5 (milieu) was the template. A fully-built chapter = `chN-tldr` (brief-card) + several `<section class="content-section">` + `chN-als` + `chN-exercises`. Each content section:
- Is one **modal tab** (the reader clones the chapter into `#modalBody` and builds a tab per `:scope > section[id]`).
- Has an `<h2>`, a `<p class="section-lead">`, and one or more `<article class="condition-block" id="chN-xxx-cbN">` — **the condition-block is the "pill"** and is what the pill-count greps.
- Pill body is EITHER a `<ul>` OR a `<div class="finding-grid">` of `<div class="finding-card">` columns (used for side-by-side contrasts, e.g. delirium vs NCD, first- vs second-gen antipsychotics).

### 22.3 Method (author → inject → verify)
1. **Read source** two-column from `/tmp/mh_source/full_layout.txt` (split col 62; content region = chapter body header → that chapter's "Application Exercises" marker, excluding "...Key" markers).
2. **Author** content sections into a marker file `/home/claude/mh_chNN_content.html` wrapped in `<!-- ==CHN-CONTENT== -->` … `<!-- ==/CHN-CONTENT== -->`.
3. **Inject** each chapter's block immediately **before** its `<section id="chN-als"`, in **reverse chapter order** (so earlier offsets never shift), with a double-inject guard (skip if a known new section id already present).
4. **Verify-before-write gate** (mandatory — see 22.4). Only on a full pass does the script write the file; otherwise it aborts with "✗ NOT written".
5. `present_files` and report.

### 22.4 The verify-before-write gate  (MH ch7–33 application of ⭐ §23.4 CORE)
The shared CORE checks (⭐ §23.4) plus these MH-enrichment specifics; every injection script recomputes and asserts, in one pass, before writing:
- **Pills delta == expected** (sum of authored condition-blocks for the batch).
- **Exercises unchanged == 161** and **ALS unchanged == 33** (enrichment must never touch question banks or templates).
- **JS errors == 0** — every non-src `<script>` block extracted and run through `node --check` via a tempfile.
- **No duplicate** `content-section` IDs; (final pass) **no chapter 1-33 missing** content sections.

This gate caught nothing catastrophic because authoring was disciplined, but it is the reason the exercise/ALS counts are provably untouched across +212 pills.

### 22.5 Sensitive-content rules (safety-first, applied throughout)
**→ See ⭐ §26.3 (canonical sensitive-content framework).** This section originally stated the policy in full during the MH ch7–33 enrichment; the per-topic rules (suicide/self-harm methods-omission, eating-disorder qualitative-only, violence recognition + mandatory reporting, sexual-assault survivor-centered framing, plus the numeric-target regex gate) were codified and superseded by §26.3. No policy change — consolidated to avoid drift.
### 22.6 Unit-by-unit results
| Unit | Chapters | Pills added | Running MH total |
|---|---|---|---|
| (start) | Ch 1-6 only | — | 128 |
| 2 — Nonpharm Therapies | Ch 7-10 | +39 | 167 |
| 3 — Psychobiologic Disorders | Ch 11-20 | +92 | 259 |

The book's Status line now records "MH Ch 7-33 enrichment complete (340 concept pills, all 33 chapters)." Storage keys, modal architecture, and the Highlights+Notes feature (PART 21) are unaffected.
