## PART 23 — PD CONVERSION (info-card/ref-table FORMAT FIX → 571 PILLS) + MN ch7 FIX

### 23.1 The discovery (what "enriching PD" actually was)
PD (Nursing Care of Children) showed **0 condition-block pills** across all 44 chapters and was assumed to need content authored from scratch. Inspection proved otherwise: **every chapter already had complete, well-organized content.** The problem was CSS. PD's dominant content container, `<div class="info-card">` (258 uses across 42 ch), its tables `<table class="ref-table">` (46 uses), and the modifier `callout-tip` (41 uses) were **never defined in the stylesheet** — so the book had been rendering its main content **unstyled**. `condition-block`, `data-table`, and base `callout` WERE defined. So "the big build" was really a pervasive **rendering bug**, the same class as MN ch7 (PART folded below) but book-wide.

**Lesson (now standard practice):** before "enriching" any book, scan for classes used in the HTML but absent from the CSS (`class="x"` with no `.x{` rule). A pill count of 0 is a symptom to investigate, not proof of missing content.

### 23.2 The fix — a two-part, content-preserving conversion
No content was authored. The build was a structural transform that simultaneously fixed rendering AND produced pills:
1. **info-card → condition-block.** `<div class="info-card"><h3>Title</h3>…</div>` → `<article class="condition-block" id="chN-cbK"><header class="condition-head"><h3 class="condition-name">Title</h3></header>…</article>`. Structurally identical; just rewrapped. Headingless info-cards become a header-less condition-block.
2. **ref-table → data-table.** Pure class rename so the existing tables pick up the defined "DATA REFERENCE TABLES" styling. No table content touched.
3. **bare-`<h3>` wrap.** Many chapters held content as bare top-level `<h3>Concept</h3>` + lists *directly under the section* (not in info-cards). After step 1 made info-cards into styled pills, these bare-h3 sections looked inconsistent (some cards, some plain). The wrap promotes each **top-level** `<h3>` and its following siblings (up to the next top-level h3/h2/article) into a condition-block. Leading section prose stays as a lead; **nested** h3s (inside lists/tables) are left alone.

### 23.3 The converter (mechanics worth keeping)
- **Balanced-tag matching, not naive regex.** `div_end()` counts nested `<div>`/`</div>`; `elem_end()` matches an arbitrary tag accounting for same-tag nesting and void/self-closing elements. The bare-h3 wrap tokenizes a section into top-level nodes so it only wraps true top-level h3s.
- **Order matters:** info-card conversion FIRST, then ref-table rename, then bare-h3 wrap — so the wrap sees the new `article`s as boundaries and won't double-wrap them.
- **ID scheme:** info-card pills get `chN-cbK`; bare-h3 pills get `{sectionId}-hK` (namespaced by section). The first attempt numbered h-pills per *section* but built the id from the *chapter*, producing collisions (ch24-h0 in two sections) — the verify-gate caught it and refused to write. Fix: namespace by section id, which is globally unique.

### 23.4 Verify-before-write gate (every batch, every write)  ⭐ CANONICAL CORE (the shared verify-gate; §20.3 / §22.4 / §24.5 / §29.5 add only workstream-specific checks on top of this)

**Shared CORE checks (every enrichment/transform write, all subjects):**
1. **Content preservation** — prove text was not silently altered. Use the strictest applicable form: text-identical (`strip(chap)==strip(new)`, tags removed + whitespace collapsed) for pure structural transforms, or word-preservation (`set(words(old))-set(words(new))==∅`) for restyling. Pick the one that matches whether the write is allowed to *add* content.
2. **No duplicate IDs** book-wide (`content-section` / `condition-block` / `ex-` / `fc-` as applicable).
3. **Count delta == expected** (pills / cards / examples added == the authored count; 0 if structure-only).
4. **Question banks untouched** — Exercises and ALS counts unchanged (enrichment must never edit question banks or templates as a side effect).
5. **JS 0 errors** — every non-src `<script>` block extracted and run through `node --check`.

Abort the write on any failure. The workstream-specific checks below sit ON TOP of this core:
- **Text-identical assertion:** `strip(chap)==strip(new)` where `strip` removes all tags and collapses whitespace. This is the core guarantee that the transform reworded/added/removed **nothing** — only structure changed. (It caught nothing on PD because the transform was disciplined, but it is the reason content preservation is provable.)
- **No duplicate IDs** book-wide (caught the ch24 collision).
- **Within-chapter redundancy** (difflib ratio ≥ 0.75–0.8) = 0.
- **Residual `info-card`/`ref-table` = 0** in the batch.
- **JS 0 errors** (`node --check` on every non-src script block).

### 23.5 Batch-by-batch (NO one-pass — standing rule)  ⭐ CANONICAL (the project-wide batch-discipline rule; other parts that restate it defer here)
Per explicit user instruction, **all multi-chapter work is done batch by batch with a check-in after each batch; a single one-pass operation across many chapters is never recommended or performed** (the user rejected it as error-prone). PD was done in: Unit 1 (ch1-11) info-card pass; system-grouped info-card passes (ch12-15, 16-19, 20-23, 24-26, 27-29, 30-34); then the bare-h3 **backfill** of ch1-34 in batches; then ch35-44 with **both** transforms. ch24 was used as a one-chapter demo of the bare-h3 wrap before rolling out.

### 23.6 "Thin chapter" investigation (and a corrected hypothesis)
Several chapters converted to very few info-card pills (ch12=2, ch18=2, ch22=3, ch24=1, ch32=0, ch34=1). An early hypothesis that these were "table-heavy" was **wrong** — inspection showed ch24 and ch34 had **0 tables**; their content was bare-h3 lists. The real cause was the bare-h3 authoring style, and the bare-h3 wrap resolved all of them (e.g., ch32 Burns 0→8, ch12 2→13, ch20 Cardiovascular became the richest chapter). Recorded here as a caution: inspect before theorizing, and state hypotheses as hypotheses.

### 23.7 Terminology note — "reference table"
"Reference table" = a literal styled `<table>` (the stylesheet's "DATA REFERENCE TABLES" component: Apgar, lochia, VEAL CHOP MINE, burn classification, etc.). It is **not** a bibliography or a central collection of references, and nothing was ever gathered or moved into one. The `ref-table`→`data-table` change was a styling rename only.

### 23.8 MN ch7 fix (same bug class, folded in)
MN had 587 pills across 25/27 chapters; ch7 (Bleeding During Pregnancy) and ch13 (Fetal Monitoring) showed 0 pills. **ch7** used orphaned `findings-grid`/`findings-col` classes (undefined) — converted each `findings-col`/`callout` (with a heading) to a `condition-block` (text-preserving), yielding **+25 pills** and fixing the unstyled rendering; a headingless callout was left as a (defined) `.callout`. **ch13 was NOT broken** — it is a deliberately custom-designed chapter (FHR tracings, three-tier severity cards, interactive mid-read checks, pattern grids) whose classes are all defined; it was correctly **left untouched**. MN → 612 pills.

### 23.9 Final state
- **MH:** 340 pills, all 33 ch (PART 22 enrichment).
- **MN:** 612 pills (ch7 fixed; ch13 intentionally custom).
- **PD:** **571 pills across all 44 ch** — 0 residual info-card/ref-table, no dup IDs, 0 within-chapter redundancy, JS clean, ~1,583 KB. Status note records the conversion.
- **Pharm:** unchanged (~108 pills in ~10 of 49 ch) — the remaining candidate; the same scan-for-undefined-classes step should run there first.
- Storage keys, modal architecture, Highlights+Notes feature, exercises, and ALS templates all unaffected throughout.

## PART 24 — PHARMACOLOGY Ch 11-49 EXPANDED-PILL AUTHORING (108 → 218 PILLS)

### 24.1 The diagnosis (a third, distinct case)
After MH (author missing content) and PD (fix a rendering bug on existing content), Pharm turned out to be a **third kind of task**. The scan that PART 23 made standard ran first and found:
- **No rendering bug.** Only one trivial used-but-undefined class (`bm-pill`, 1 use); all content containers (`condition-block`, `finding-grid`, `finding-card`, `brief-card`, `condition-tag`, `data-table`) are defined. So, unlike PD, nothing was broken.
- **10 of 49 chapters complete, 39 half-built.** ch1-10 had a TL;DR (brief-card) PLUS multiple expanded `content-section` pills. ch11-49 had a **rich TL;DR (brief-grid of drug-class columns) + ALS + exercises but NO expanded content-section pills**. (A measurement artifact briefly suggested they were empty — "content≈0 chars" — because the measurement looked between the first `content-section` and `chN-als`, which were adjacent; the actual content lived in the `brief-card` TL;DR. Inspecting the raw markup corrected this.)

**Implication:** there was **no content-preserving shortcut** (unlike PD). The expanded pills genuinely did not exist — only condensed TL;DR summaries did. Bringing ch11-49 to ch1-10 depth required **authoring from the source PDF**, like MH — the largest single task in the suite. This was surfaced to the user as an explicit scope decision (author vs. leave as-is vs. shallow TL;DR→pill conversion); the user chose authoring after a one-chapter pilot.

### 24.2 Pilot-first (ch20)
Per the MH precedent, a single chapter (ch20, Medications Affecting Blood Pressure) was authored first and presented for approval of **depth and house style** before any rollout. The pilot established the template: 5 content-sections, ~10 drug-class pills, each pill = mechanism → therapeutic uses → key/dangerous complications → contraindications → interactions → nursing/administration. Approved, then applied to the remaining 38 chapters.

### 24.3 Pharm house style (matches ch1-10)
Each pill:
```html
<article class="condition-block" id="chN-{section}-cbK">
  <header class="condition-head">
    <h3 class="condition-name">Drug / class name</h3>
    <span class="condition-tag">short label</span>   <!-- Pharm-specific; ch1-10 use it -->
  </header>
  <p>Mechanism…</p>
  <div class="finding-grid"><div class="finding-card"><h4>Uses</h4><ul>…</ul></div>…</div>
  <!-- or a plain <ul> for shorter pills -->
</article>
```
The `condition-tag` span is Pharm's signature (drug class / prototype / schedule). New content-sections were inserted **between the TL;DR and `chN-als`** (the TL;DR was left intact as the summary; the new pills are the depth beneath it). Section ids are topic-based (`ch20-raas`, `ch20-ccb`, …), pill ids namespaced by section (`ch20-raas-cb0`).

### 24.4 Source extraction — word-coordinate column split
The Pharm PDF (Edition 8.0, 429 pages) is two-column. A fixed-character column split (as first attempted) drifts line-to-line and garbles the right column. The reliable method:
- **`colread(page)`** — `page.extract_words(use_text_flow=True)`, split words by `x0 < page.width/2` into left/right buckets, regroup each bucket into lines by rounded `top`. Clean two-column separation.
- **`cand(ch, keyword)`** — find a chapter's PDF pages: pages whose uppercased text contains `f"CHAPTER {ch} "` AND the title keyword AND **≤ 3 distinct chapter numbers** (the ≤3 filter excludes the TOC/index pages, which list every chapter — an early bug grabbed page 6, the TOC, until this filter was added). Take the **longest contiguous run** of matching pages (the body).
- Saved per chapter to `/tmp/chNN_clean.txt`. (Note: a few chapters' running headers don't repeat the keyword on every page, so `cand` sometimes returns 1 page; domain knowledge + the chapter's own TL;DR filled the gaps without fabricating.)

### 24.5 Batch-by-batch + verify-gate (16 batches)
Standing rule honored (⭐ §23.5): **no one-pass.** ~2-3 chapters per batch, check-in after each. Order followed the unit grouping (Nervous System → Respiratory → Cardiovascular → Hematologic → GI → Reproductive → Joint & Bone → Pain → Endocrine → Immune → Infection → Other). Every write passed the gate or was aborted:
- pills delta == expected;
- exercises unchanged (**251** throughout) and ALS untouched;
- no duplicate condition-block ids book-wide;
- within-chapter near-duplicate scan (difflib ≥ 0.75) == 0;
- JS 0 errors (`node --check` on every non-src `<script>`).
Injection used reverse chapter order within a batch (so earlier offsets stay valid) and a double-inject guard (skip if a sentinel section id already present).

### 24.6 Faithfulness & sensitive-content discipline  (→ ⭐ §26.3 for the canonical sensitive-content framework)
- **Paraphrase, never copy** (copyright). Pills restate ATI content in our own words.
- **Medication-reference numbers ARE included** (therapeutic ranges, hold parameters): digoxin apical pulse hold < 60/min, verapamil hold pulse < 50/SBP < 90, INR 2-3, aPTT 1.5-2×, K⁺ 3.5-5.0, insulin onset/peak windows, lithium-style ranges. These are distinct from the eating-disorder numeric rule (which bars weight/BMI/calorie targets) — pharmacology safety numbers are essential and retained.
- **No fabrication.** ch14 ("Eye and Ear Disorders") has no substantive otic drug content in the source → authored glaucoma only, no invented ear meds. Where the source defers (ch20 TL;DR cross-references CCB/beta-blocker detail to ch22-23), the cross-reference was honored: ch20's beta-blocker pill is tagged "Detailed in Ch 22-23," and the full treatment was authored in ch22-23 — avoiding cross-chapter duplication.
- Child/adolescent psych meds (ch11) and substance-use (ch12) overlap MH Ch 25-26 by topic but were authored independently from the Pharm source in Pharm style; growth/appetite effects kept qualitative ("monitor height/weight against baseline").

### 24.7 Result
**Pharm: 218 pills across all 49 chapters** (from 108 in 10 ch). Whole-book certification: every chapter carded, no chapters without pills, no duplicate ids, 0 within-chapter redundancy (218 scanned), exercises 251, JS clean. Status note records the authoring.

### 24.8 Suite status after this session ⚠️ HISTORICAL SNAPSHOT (frozen at the time of that session — for current counts/push status see the ⭐ MASTER CURRENT STATE block at top and `SESSION_VERIFICATION_CHECKLIST.md`)
- **MH** 340 pills (PART 22 enrichment) · **MN** 612 (ch7 fix, PART 23) · **PD** 571 (full conversion, PART 23) · **Pharm** 218 (authoring, this PART). All four books complete.
- The three task archetypes are now documented end to end: **author missing content** (MH, Pharm), **fix a rendering bug on existing content** (PD, MN ch7), and the **scan-first diagnosis** (PART 23) that tells them apart. Always scan for used-but-undefined CSS classes AND compare chapter structure to the book's own complete chapters before deciding which archetype applies.

## PART 25 — FOUR-SUBJECT GAP AUDIT + ALL FIXES (MH Flashcards & Templates built, PD ch17, Pharm dactinomycin, MH Hub wired)

This part documents a full **gap audit** across all four subjects (does each tool cover its source?) and every fix that followed. Net result: MH went from two tools to the **full four-tool suite**, PD's one real content gap was closed, and Pharm reached 162/162 prototype coverage. It also captures two reusable build techniques: the **flashcard shell-clone** and the **Templates generator** against the intricate ATL engine.

### 25.1 The audit — method per subject (one source PDF at a time)
For each subject, check all four: (1) source topics vs Book pills, (2) Flashcard per-chapter coverage, (3) Template coverage, (4) structural gaps. Two source-topic extraction methods depending on the TOC:
- **TOC-subtopic method** (MN, MH): ATI TOCs sometimes list subtopics under each chapter (MN did richly; MH/PD mostly chapter-level). Parse lines ending in a page number that aren't UNIT/SECTION/CHAPTER headers → authoritative subtopic checklist → check each distinctive keyword against the Book chapter text.
- **12pt-heading method** (PD, MH): when the TOC is chapter-level only, extract chapter-body headings by font size. Body is **8pt**; headings are **12pt** (`char['size']>=10.5`, ≥3 big chars and >60% of the line). Filter to heading-like phrases (≤6 words, no sentence words like is/are/the/should, not mostly-lowercase). **Noisy** — column-merge artifacts fuse adjacent headers ("mEDICATIONSCOMPLICATIONS", "eyeseaRs", "IntussusceptionAppendicitis"); verify each flagged term individually against the Book before believing it's a gap.
- Tool coverage from the HTML is reliable: flashcards keyed by `ch:'chN'` (count per chapter; flag any with 0); templates are ATL collections (count by type).

### 25.2 Audit findings
- **MN — NO GAPS.** 27 ch, **97/97 TOC subtopics** covered, 612 pills; Flashcards 122 (all ch); Templates 201 ATLs.
- **PD — ch17 gap (real).** Source ch17 lists nine respiratory illnesses; Book had six. **Missing: nasopharyngitis (common cold), allergic rhinitis, bacterial tracheitis.** Inherited from the pre-conversion book (the content-preserving conversion can't add what wasn't there). The "ANTINEOPLASTICS" heading flag was a **false alarm** — leukemia/lymphoma lives in its own ch40 (the audit's first ch40 check used a sloppy `id="ch40"` selector that matched a nav link and returned 0; the proper `<section class="chapter" id="ch40">` selector showed leukemia 22×).
- **Pharm — essentially clean.** **161/162** source `SELECT PROTOTYPE MEDICATION` drugs covered; only **dactinomycin** unnamed (its class, antitumor antibiotics, was covered via doxorubicin). Flashcards 260 (all ch; ch11-49 carry 207 — never had the book's old thin-upper-chapters problem). Templates ch1-49.
- **MH — Book complete (340 pills, 33 ch, all topics; the 13 heading flags were all merge artifacts/hyphenation), but NO Flashcards and NO Templates.** The biggest gap by far.

### 25.3 PD ch17 fix
Pulled source content with the column-aware extractor; nasopharyngitis and allergic rhinitis are substantive sections, bacterial tracheitis only named in the intro list. Added **3 pills** to the `ch17-other` ("Other respiratory infections") section (ids `ch17-nasopharyngitis`, `ch17-allergic-rhinitis`, `ch17-tracheitis`) → PD **574 pills**; added **2 flashcards** (`fc-ch17-nasopharyngitis`, `fc-ch17-allergic-rhinitis`) after the croup card → PD Flashcards **361**. Verify-gate: pill delta +3, exercises unchanged (218), no dup ids, within-chapter redundancy 0, JS clean.

### 25.4 MH Flashcards build — the shell-clone technique (108 cards)
Flashcards are a **reusable engine**; only the card data and a handful of shell parameters differ between subjects. Method:
1. **Split the peer file** (cloned PD Flashcards) at `var STARTER_DECK = [ … ]` — the card array (PD's was 168 KB at a balanced-bracket span). Everything before/after is the shell. `var cards = []` is a runtime buffer; the real definitions live in STARTER_DECK; cards render via `loadStarterDeck()`/`getDeck()`.
2. **Card schema:** `{ id:'fc-chN-slug', ch:'chN', type:'concept'|'calc', anchor:'chN', q:'…', a:'…' }`.
3. **Shell swaps** (apply to pre+post shell): there are **TWO unit filter UIs** to swap — the **sidebar** `sb-nav-item data-quick-filter="unit"` block AND the **filter-chip** `data-filter-group="unit"` block — plus the **`chapterUnit(chNum)`** JS range function, plus the **`filter-chips-numeric data-filter-group="chapter"`** chips (PD 1-44 → MH 1-33). Then theme (`#0284c7`→`#65a30d`, `#0369a1`→`#4d7c0f`, `2,132,199`→`101,163,13`), title, `atipd`→`atimh`, book links PD→MH.
4. **MH units:** foundations 1-6 · therapies 7-10 · disorders 11-20 · psychopharm 21-26 · special-pop 27-28 · emergencies 29-33.
5. **Populate by unit, batch by batch** (6 batches → 108 cards: 19/15/30/20/8/16). Each batch: append before STARTER_DECK's closing `]`, verify card delta, no dup ids, JS clean.
6. **Sensitive-content gates:** eating-disorder cards ran a **numeric-safety scan** (no weight/BMI/calorie/vital numbers — passed); Unit 6 ran a **suicide-method scan** (no methods named — passed). Medication-reference numbers (lithium 0.6-1.2 mEq/L, EPS/NMS, MAOI-tyramine) ARE included — distinct from the ED rule.

### 25.5 MH Templates build — the ATL engine + generator (45 ATLs)
The Templates file is the most intricate tool (peer PD is 1.57 MB, 167 cards). **Architecture** (reverse-engineered):
- `#templatePool` holds one **`<section id="TYPE" class="template-section">`** container per ATL type; inside each is an `example-stack` of **`<div class="example-card" id="ex-chN-slug">`** cards.
- Each card = an `example-header` (title, chapter link, Filled/Blank toggle) + a `<dl class="template-meta">` (Student Name, type-specific label, Review Module Chapter) + a **grid** of `<div class="tp-box"><h3>FIELD</h3><div class="content">…</div></div>`.
- **Three regions must stay consistent:** the templatePool **sections**, the **accordions** (`<div class="unit-accordion" data-template-id="TYPE" id="TYPE-acc">` with `0 / N studied` counts + progress bars), and the **sidebar groups** (`<div class="sb-tpl-group" data-tpl="TYPE">` with `sb-tpl-example` links). On init the JS does `pool.querySelector('#'+templateId)` per accordion, reads that section's `.example-card`s, and builds the navigator — so **section id == accordion data-template-id == sidebar data-tpl**, and every sidebar link href must match a card id.
- **Grid field layouts** (extract once, reuse): **bc-grid** (Basic Concept) = Related Content / Underlying Principles / Nursing Interventions. **sd-grid** (System Disorder) = 14 fields (Alterations in Health, Pathophysiology, Health Promotion, Risk Factors, Expected Findings, Laboratory Tests, Diagnostic Procedures, Safety Considerations, Complications, Nursing Care, Medications, Therapeutic Procedures, Client Education, Interprofessional Care). **med-grid** (Medication) = 9 fields (Expected Pharmacological Action, Therapeutic Use, Complications, Contraindications/Precautions, Interactions, Evaluation, Administration, Nursing Interventions, Client Education) + a "Category Class" meta row. **tp-grid** (Therapeutic & Diagnostic Procedure) = Description / Indications / Interpretation of Findings / Nursing Interventions (pre, intra, post) / Potential Complications / Client Education.

**Build method (generator, not hand-edit):**
1. **Detect the three region boundaries** by consuming balanced sibling blocks: 7 `sb-tpl-group` (div), 8 `unit-accordion` (div), and the `template-section`s (**8, not 7** — there's a trailing "Concept Analysis (placeholder)" `<section>` after the 7 real ones; extend the section bound to swallow it or you'll be left with a stray 6th section).
2. **Generator functions** emit card / section / accordion / sidebar-group from MH ATL data, guaranteeing the 3-way consistency.
3. **Excise PD's three regions, inject MH's**, replacing high-index region first so offsets stay valid; then theme/storage/title/book swaps.
4. **5 MH ATL types** (Nursing Skill & Growth-and-Development dropped — not core to MH): Basic Concept 10, System Disorder 11, Medication 12, Therapeutic Procedure 8, Diagnostic Procedure 4 = **45 ATLs**.
5. **Batch by type**, injecting cards into the type's empty `example-stack`, links into its sidebar group, and updating three counts (banner "Active · N examples", accordion "0 / N studied", sidebar `sb-tpl-count`). Verify each: card delta, no dup ids, JS clean, and (System Disorder) the ED numeric scan on the eating-disorders card.
6. **Final integrity check:** sidebar-link count == card count, every link has a matching card and vice-versa, 0 PD residue, lime theme present.

### 25.6 MH Hub wiring + Pharm dactinomycin
- **MH Hub:** peer Hubs have three `<a class="tool-card">` (Book, Templates, Flashcards); MH had only Book (its Flashcards/Templates were never built, and the lone `href="#"` is just the JS-populated pickup panel, not a broken nav link). Ported the PD Templates + Flashcards tool-cards, swapped PD→MH, corrected the Templates eyebrow to "45 worked examples" and its description to MH's five types. (Optional remaining polish: the pickup-panel resume cards for fc/templates — peers have 10 pickup-cards, MH has 8.)
- **Pharm dactinomycin:** a content add (not a pill), into the ch42 "Antitumor antibiotics & mitotic inhibitors" pill — added dactinomycin beside doxorubicin in the bullet and the condition-tag. Pills unchanged (218); now 162/162 prototypes covered.

### 25.7 Reusable techniques & gotchas
- **Apostrophe escaping in `python3 << 'PYEOF'` heredocs:** content goes into HTML (Templates) or JS (flashcards). In single-quoted Python strings, `\\'` = backslash + closing-quote (SyntaxError). For HTML content use the entity **`&rsquo;`** (cleanest); for JS-string card content use a single-backslash `\'`. This bit the build twice — standardize on `&rsquo;` for any authored apostrophe.
- **Balanced-block excision** beats regex for big nested HTML regions; consume N sibling `<div>`/`<section>` by depth-counting, and **verify the count inside the captured span** before replacing.
- **Sloppy id selectors lie:** `c.find('id="ch40"')` matches `href="#ch40"` nav links. Always anchor on the full element (`<section class="chapter" id="ch40">`).
- **Heading-extraction is a lead, not a verdict:** every flagged "gap" must be re-checked as a literal substring (and under synonyms — nasopharyngitis ⇆ "common cold") in the Book before authoring.

Triggered by the user noticing **Mental Health missing from the landing page**. ### The index bug
`index.html` has a `<section class="hero">` followed by `<section class="subjects">` (the card grid). - **Books:** every `<section class="chapter">` falls inside `#chapterPool`…`</main>`; every `<article class="condition-block">` falls inside some chapter span; no duplicate chapter ids. All 4 clean (MN 27/612, PD 44/574, Pharm 49/218, MH 33/340).
- **Flashcards:** every `id:'fc-…'` lies within the `STARTER_DECK` balanced-bracket span; no duplicate ids. All 4 clean.

Fix: cloned the last `sb-tpl-group`, swapped `data-tpl`/`data-toggle-tpl`/num(08)/name/count(2), and listed the 2 example links. orphan 2→0.

### Standing rule added to the verify-gate
For any Templates build/edit, assert the invariant **`linkids == cardids`** (no dead links, no orphan cards) AND **every example-card sits inside a `template-section`** — alongside the existing checks (JS `node --check`, no dup ids, count deltas). For Books, assert **chapters ⊂ chapterPool** and **pills ⊂ chapters**; for Flashcards, **cards ⊂ STARTER_DECK**. The MH tools built this session already satisfied all invariants (0/0); the scan's value was catching the **older peer files**. Net: whole suite structurally clean.

#### The `/tmp/tplgen.py` generator (recreate if session resets)
Three public functions:
- `build_card(typ, ch, slug, name, chtitle, boxes, category_class=None)` — returns full card HTML matching the exact existing structure for `typ` in `{bc, sd, med, tp}`. `boxes` is a dict keyed by box label → HTML content (already wrapped in `<p>`/`<ul>`).
- `deepen(PATH, specs)` — regenerates existing cards in place by id. Preserves card-count invariant; rebuilds the card wrapper (header, meta `dl`, grid) from spec so chapter titles get fixed in `example-source` and `always-show` meta simultaneously with content deepening. **Write-guard:** card count must stay equal; no duplicate ids; all inline scripts pass `node --check`. On failure: `✗ ...` returned, disk untouched.
- `add_new(PATH, specs)` — for the 6 new chapters. Each spec includes `group` (sidebar `data-tpl`). Appends card HTML at EOF (MH file's card list runs to EOF — there's no `</main></body></html>` close in this file, matching the original PD-cloned shell). Then for each new card: inserts `<a href="#ex-chN-slug" class="sb-tpl-example">Name</a>` before its sidebar group's `</div>` close, and bumps that group's `sb-tpl-count`. **Write-guard:** card count must grow by `len(specs)`; no duplicate ids; **for every sidebar group, `sb-tpl-count == count of `class="sb-tpl-example"` actually inside that group`**; `node --check` on all scripts. (This is the standing invariant added in §25.9, now enforced by the generator at write time, not after the fact.)

Box label sets per type (the source-of-truth ordering used by `build_card`):
- **bc** (basic-concept) — meta label `Concept`, grid `bc-grid`, 3 boxes: `Related Content`, `Underlying Principles`, `Nursing Interventions`.
- **tp** (therapeutic/diagnostic-procedure) — meta `Procedure Name`, grid `tp-grid`, 6 `tp-box` with classes `description / indications / considerations / outcomes / complications / client-edu` matching labels `Description of Procedure / Indications / Nursing Interventions (pre, intra, post) / Interpretation of Findings / Potential Complications / Client Education`.
- **med** (medication) — meta `Medication` + `Category Class`, grid `med-grid` = `tpl-group purpose-group` (label `Purpose of Medication`, 2 boxes: `Expected Pharmacological Action`, `Therapeutic Use`) + `med-body > med-col-left` (4 boxes: `Complications`, `Contraindications/Precautions`, `Interactions`, `Evaluation of Medication Effectiveness`) + `med-col-right` (3 boxes with classes `''/med-ni/med-ce`: `Medication Administration`, `Nursing Interventions`, `Client Education`).
- **sd** (system-disorder) — meta `Disorder/Disease Process`, grid `sd-grid` = `sd-top-row` (3 boxes: `Alterations in Health (Diagnosis)`, `Pathophysiology Related to Client Problem`, `Health Promotion and Disease Prevention`) + `sd-middle` containing `tpl-group assessment-group` (4 boxes: `Risk Factors`, `Expected Findings`, `Laboratory Tests`, `Diagnostic Procedures`), `tpl-group safety-group` (2 boxes: `Safety Considerations`, `Complications`), `tpl-group patient-care-group` (5 boxes: `Nursing Care`, `Medications`, `Therapeutic Procedures`, `Client Education`, `Interprofessional Care`).

### 26.3 Sensitive-content framework — codified rules per topic  ⭐ CANONICAL (single source of truth for sensitive-content policy; §20.6 / §22.5 / §24.6 / §41.3 / §42.6 defer to this)
The MH content forces a class of writing rule the other three subjects largely don't: there are a small number of topics where **adding detail makes the content worse, not better, for vulnerable readers**. Rules applied consistently across MH Flashcards, MH Templates, and MH Book throughout this session (and §26.4):

| Topic | Affected anchors | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Suicide / self-harm | ch13 MDD, ch16 BPD self-injury, ch28 youth, ch30 Suicide | Risk-assessment + protective interventions only. **Never name methods.** Means restriction kept GENERAL ("remove potentially harmful items from environment", "restrict access to means of harm") — never name specific items. Asking directly **does not increase risk**; never dismiss a verbal statement. Black-box warning for SSRIs in adolescents; energy-returns-before-mood-lifts risk window. |
| Eating disorders | ch19 | **QUALITATIVE only.** Behavioral + physical findings (restriction, lanugo, bradycardia, dental erosion, Russell's sign, parotid swelling) and electrolyte/cardiac risk (hypokalemia, refeeding syndrome by electrolyte shifts) **OK as clinical lab references**. **No weight, BMI, or calorie targets anywhere.** Refeeding syndrome described by physiology, no numbers. |
| Substance-use pharm | ch18, ch26 | Standard pharmacology (disulfiram, naltrexone, acamprosate, methadone, buprenorphine, naloxone, NRT, varenicline, bupropion) is appropriate clinical content. "Lethal in overdose" for TCAs is a clinical safety warning, not a method instruction — context disambiguates. |
| Family/community violence | ch32 | Recognition indicators + mandatory reporting framing (nurses are mandatory reporters of suspected child and vulnerable-adult abuse) + trauma-informed care + conceptual safety planning. Survivor never to blame. No graphic detail. |
| Sexual assault | ch33 | Survivor-centered framing. **Informed consent before forensic exam (SANE).** Preserve evidence only if survivor consents. Address injuries, pregnancy, STI prophylaxis. Recognize rape-trauma syndrome (acute → reorganization). "All responses are normal; the assault is not the survivor's fault." No graphic detail of the assault itself. |

Regex scan as a safety net (added to verification step for sensitive content): `BMI\s*[<>≤≥]?\s*\d|weight\s*[<>≤≥]\s*\d` (eating numbers), `\d+\s*(?:k?cal|calorie)` (calorie numbers), `\b(hanging|firearm|overdose|jumping|cutting tools|sharps|cords|belts|shoelaces|plastic bags?|ligature)\b` (method words). The method-word scan **false-positives** on "lethal in overdose" (TCA), "naloxone reverses overdose" (SUD), and "no sharps access" (milieu therapy) — those are appropriate clinical contexts and the scan output requires manual disambiguation, not blind removal.

Asking directly about suicidal thoughts does not increase risk."), Nursing Interventions ("Use a validated tool — e.g., the C-SSRS — to structure questions about ideation, plan, intent, and prior behavior"), Interpretation ("The C-SSRS classifies risk on a continuum — passive wishes for death → active ideation → active ideation with plan and intent → recent suicidal behavior — and this classification guides the intensity of safety measures.").
- **MH Flashcards `fc-ch30-c-ssrs`** — new focused concept card. Q: *What is the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS)?* A: brief description + the same continuum + "Asking directly does not increase risk."
- **MH Book `ch30-assessment-cb1`** — expanded existing bullet on "use a standardized tool (SAD PERSONS scale)" → now reads "...use a standardized tool such as the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) or the SAD PERSONS scale", and added one new bullet describing what the C-SSRS measures and the same continuum framing. **SAD PERSONS retained** (ATI-faithful — both tools now named, student sees the more contemporary C-SSRS alongside the older one).

### 26.7 Reusable techniques captured from this session
- **For multi-card structural edits where every card needs the same shape:** prefer a Python generator that regenerates the whole card from a spec dict, with a single write-guard (count delta + id uniqueness + JS check), over per-card str_replace. `tplgen.deepen()` is the canonical pattern — survives a session reset because the box label sets and grid structure are encoded once, content lives in the call site.
- **For adding new cards that affect sidebars:** the generator must update three places atomically — the main card HTML, the sidebar group's `<a>` link list, and the group's `sb-tpl-count` — and verify the invariant `count == links` per group before writing. `tplgen.add_new()` is the canonical pattern.
- **For multi-batch authoring sessions over many hours:** the harness sometimes echoes stale `ask_user_input` answers (e.g., re-surfacing "Continue — batch 2" after batch 9 has shipped). Standing rule: **interpret stale echoes as harness artifacts, not as user direction to re-execute completed work.** Acknowledge the echo briefly and re-surface the actual open question. This happened multiple times this session and was correctly handled each time.
- **Spot-check pattern for sensitive content:** after building, extract the rendered text content (HTML stripped) and re-read it as if a vulnerable reader. Then run the regex scan as a second pass. The combination catches both content-level issues (the framework was applied correctly) and lexical leaks (a method word slipped in).

## PART 27 — MH TEMPLATES 8-TYPE PARITY + CANONICAL ORDERING RULE (correction to §26.2)
This part corrects a real gap missed in §26.2 and adds a project-wide standing rule about template-type completeness and ordering that the verify-gate must now enforce.

### 27.1 The gap PART 26 missed
PART 26 documented the MH Templates final state as **5 sidebar groups** and treated that as complete. It wasn't. The 5-group state is a leftover from MH's PD-clone origin (PD itself only has 7 of the 8 types, MH was further reduced). The **8 canonical ATI Active Learning Template types** are defined in §18 (BC / DP / GD / Med / NS / SD / TP / CA — corresponding to ATI source numbers A1, A3, A5, A7, A9, A11, A13, A15). MH was missing **GD (Growth and Development)**, **NS (Nursing Skill)**, and **CA (Concept Analysis)**, and the 5 groups it did have were not in canonical order.

This was caught by the user noticing it, not by the verify-gate. The gate now adds that check (§27.3).

### 27.2 Fix applied: full 8-type parity + canonical ordering + sequential labels
The MH Templates sidebar is now:

| Position | data-tpl | Display name | ATI src | Cards |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | basic-concept | Basic Concept | A1 | 13 |
| 02 | diagnostic-procedure | Diagnostic Procedure | A3 | 4 |
| 03 | growth-development | Growth and Development | A5 | 1 (new) |
| 04 | medication | Medication | A7 | 12 |
| 05 | nursing-skill | Nursing Skill | A9 | 1 (new) |
| 06 | system-disorder | System Disorder | A11 | 12 |
| 07 | therapeutic-procedure | Therapeutic Procedure | A13 | 10 |
| 08 | concept-analysis | Concept Analysis | A15 | 1 (new) |

**Total: 54 cards** (was 51). The displayed sidebar numbers are sequential `01..08` (matching MN's pattern), not the ATI source numbers (A1..A15); those source numbers are reference metadata only.

#### The three new cards
- **GD `ex-ch1-lifespan-mh` — Mental Health Across the Lifespan** (Developmental Stage = "Lifespan — Adolescent to Older Adult"). All 9 GD boxes filled, including the nested Health-Promotion-parent + 4-children structure (Immunizations / Health Screening / Nutrition / Injury Prevention). Health Screening box references the **C-SSRS** for adolescent suicide-risk screening.
- **NS `ex-ch31-de-escalation` — De-escalation Techniques** (Skill Name = "De-escalation Techniques"). Uses `.tp-grid` with the NS-specific 5-box label set (Description of Skill / Indications / Outcomes/Evaluation / Potential Complications / Nursing Interventions). Pairs naturally with the existing ch31 Seclusion-and-Restraint TP card — de-escalation is the less-restrictive step that precedes any restraint use.
- **CA `ex-mental-health-concept` — Mental Health** (the concept itself). Uses `.ca-grid` with the 5 CA-specific box classes (`defining`, `antecedents`, `consequences`, `related`, `exemplars`). **Note id format:** CA cards use `ex-{slug}` with no `chN-` prefix, matching MN's `ex-attachment` convention.

#### Generator additions
The `/tmp/tplgen.py` generator now supports three additional types and one new function:
- `build_card(typ='gd', ...)` — 9-box GD card with the `health-promotion-group` nested structure (`hp-parent` + `hp-connectors` + 4 child boxes), `Developmental Stage` meta label.
- `build_card(typ='ns', ...)` — 5-box NS card reusing `.tp-grid`, `Skill Name` meta label, NS-specific box classes (`description / indications / outcomes / complications / nursing-interventions`).
- `build_card(typ='ca', ...)` — 5-box CA card with `.ca-grid`, **2-row meta** (Student Name + Concept Analysis with `always-show`, **no Review Module Chapter row**), free-form example-source text passed via `chtitle`.
- `reorder_groups(PATH)` — rebuilds sidebar in canonical order (`CANONICAL_GROUPS` constant), adds empty placeholder groups for any missing types, renumbers `sb-tpl-num` sequentially `01..NN`, preserves each existing group's example links + count. Write-guard: every canonical group present, every group's `sb-tpl-count == actual `class="sb-tpl-example"` count`, JS `node --check` clean.
- `_build_cid(spec)` helper — returns `ex-{slug}` for typ='ca', otherwise `ex-ch{ch}-{slug}`. Used by `add_new` for both id-collision check and sidebar-link insertion.

#### Bug found and fixed in `reorder_groups`
First run failed at the verify-gate because the examples-extraction regex was looking inside a substring that didn't include the examples-list closing `</div>`. The non-greedy outer regex `(.*?)</div>\s*</div>` consumes both closing divs, leaving the inner extraction unable to find its own `</div>`. Fix: extract examples from `m.group(0)` (full match including both closing divs) rather than from `m.group(2)` (just the inner span). The write-guard correctly aborted on first run → disk untouched → safe re-run after patch.

### 27.3 New standing rule for the verify-gate — template-type completeness + canonical order
**For any Templates file, the verify-gate must assert all of the following invariants** (in addition to those from §25.9):

```
SIDEBAR_GROUP_INVARIANTS (Templates files):
  1. Every canonical type IS represented as a sidebar group, even if its count is 0.
     canonical_set = {basic-concept, diagnostic-procedure, growth-development,
                      medication, nursing-skill, system-disorder,
                      therapeutic-procedure, concept-analysis}
     for tpl in canonical_set: assert f'data-tpl="{tpl}"' in file
  2. Sidebar groups appear in canonical ATI order (the order above —
     corresponding to ATI source A1/A3/A5/A7/A9/A11/A13/A15).
  3. sb-tpl-num values are sequential "01" through "0N" matching the
     DOM order of the groups, NOT the ATI source numbers.
  4. For each group: sb-tpl-count == count of <a class="sb-tpl-example"> inside that group.
  5. main-desc text says "eight standardized ATI Active Learning templates" iff
     all 8 canonical groups are present (text and structure must agree).
```

A type that has zero cards for a subject is still represented as a sidebar group with `count=0` — this preserves the visible 8-type scaffold and matches the canonical structure (the Pharm Templates `growth-development(0)` group is the precedent for this pattern; it's structurally correct, just empty).

### 27.6 Addendum — main-area `unit-accordion` block is a SECOND structural surface (correction to §27)
After §27.1–27.5, the MH Templates file still rendered incorrectly to the user, showing only **5 unit-accordion sections** in the main content area with **sequential page labels A1–A5** (wrong). The sidebar work in §27.2 was correct as far as it went, but **§27 missed that there is a SECOND structural surface that must also be kept in canonical sync**: the main-content `<div class="unit-accordion" data-template-id="...">` block that contains the visible accordion headers (the ones with `unit-title`, `unit-pages`, and `unit-count`).

This block is what students actually see when they scroll the main content. The sidebar is navigation; the main-area accordions are content. A correct Templates file must keep BOTH surfaces in canonical sync.

#### What the main-area accordion controls
Each accordion has:
- `data-template-id="<tpl>"` — the type identifier (must match a sidebar `data-tpl`)
- `id="<tpl>-acc"` on the outer div, with related ids `<tpl>-count`, `<tpl>-bar`, `<tpl>-barpartial`
- `unit-title` = sequential **"N · Display Name"** (matches sidebar `sb-tpl-num` numbering, 1–8)
- `unit-pages` = **canonical ATI source page** — `A1, A3, A5, A7, A9, A11, A13, A15` (odd-numbered, matching the ATI book layout in §18). **Not** sequential A1–A8.
- `unit-count` = `0 / <N> studied` where `<N>` matches the count of cards for that type (synced with sidebar `sb-tpl-count`)
- An **empty `<div class="unit-body"></div>`** — at runtime, JS moves cards from the hidden template pool into this body based on `data-template-id`

#### Expanded standing rule (supersedes §27.3 single-surface version)
**For any Templates file, the verify-gate must assert all of the following invariants across BOTH structural surfaces:**

```
TEMPLATE_FILE_INVARIANTS (Templates files):
  S1. Sidebar contains all 8 canonical sb-tpl-groups in canonical order
      (basic-concept → diagnostic-procedure → growth-development → medication
       → nursing-skill → system-disorder → therapeutic-procedure → concept-analysis)
      with sb-tpl-num "01".."08" sequential.
  S2. Main-content area contains all 8 canonical unit-accordion sections in the same
      canonical order, with unit-title "1 · ..." through "8 · ..." sequential.
  S3. unit-pages values are the canonical ATI source pages:
      A1, A3, A5, A7, A9, A11, A13, A15 — odd numbers, NOT sequential.
  S4. For each type: sb-tpl-count == count(class="sb-tpl-example" inside that group)
      == count target in unit-count "0 / N studied" == actual count of example-cards
      whose group-membership resolves to that type.
  S5. main-desc text says "eight standardized ATI Active Learning templates" iff
      both S1 and S2 hold (text and structure agree across BOTH surfaces).
```

A subject with zero cards for a type still represents the type in BOTH surfaces (sidebar group with count=0, AND unit-accordion with `0 / 0 studied`). The 8-type scaffold is structural, not content-dependent.

#### What this means in practice
Adding or removing template types is a **two-surface edit**, not a one-surface edit. The `tplgen.py` generator's `reorder_groups()` function (§27.2) only handles surface S1. A companion `rebuild_unit_accordions()` operation is now also required for surface S2 — same canonical order, same per-type counts, but with `unit-pages` set from the canonical A1/A3/A5/A7/A9/A11/A13/A15 lookup (NOT from any sequential counter).

A future `tplgen.py` upgrade should bundle both surface edits behind a single `sync_canonical_structure(PATH)` call that fails fast if either surface diverges from canonical.

#### Also: a regex gotcha logged for the gate
The naive dup-id check `re.findall(r'id="([^"]+)"', file)` produces false positives because **`data-template-id="X"` matches the substring `id="X"`** (the `data-template-` prefix doesn't break the regex). Use `re.findall(r'\sid="([^"]+)"', file)` (whitespace-prefixed) to require that the `id` attribute be at a word boundary. The same applies to CSS selectors like `[data-template-id="X"]` — they also produce false positives without the boundary. Caught in this part during a `rebuild_unit_accordions` write-guard run.

### 27.7 Addendum — MH Templates was a structurally incomplete clone (file-completeness invariant)
Triggered by the user reporting that accordions in MH Templates couldn't be clicked after §27.6's main-area rebuild. Investigation revealed the MH Templates file had been missing all JavaScript and the closing `</body></html>` tags since whenever it was originally cloned from PD — the file was 247K vs MN's 1.3MB and PD's 1.6MB. CSS-only behaviors (Filled/Blank visual state via `[data-mode="blank"]` selectors, layout, sidebar appearance) worked without JS, so no one noticed until an interactive element was clicked.

#### What was missing
- All 4 `<script>` blocks (~54K total in MN/PD): main UI (theme, sidebar, mode-toggle handlers, card-pool-to-accordion population), template filter state + studied tracking, hash focus / last-template, print button injection.
- The closing `</body>` and `</html>` tags.

#### Fix applied
Extracted MN Templates' full tail from the first `<script>` through `</html>` (54,112 chars). Adapted for MH by swapping the single subject-specific storage key:
```
nur2460_atimnTemplates_progress  →  nur2460_atimhTemplates_progress
```
(occurs in two places — the per-example progress key and the same key under STUDIED_KEY in the filter logic). All four scripts then passed `node --check`. Wrote the adapted tail to MH after the last card.

#### New file-completeness invariant added to the verify-gate
**For every HTML output file (Books, Hubs, Flashcards, Templates):**
```
FILE_COMPLETENESS_INVARIANTS:
  F1. file ends with </body></html> (with a newline) — closing tags present.
  F2. <script> tags count >= the canonical count for the file type
      (Templates files: ≥ 4 non-src scripts cloned from MN/PD pattern).
  F3. file size is within ~30% of the canonical reference file for its type
      (Templates: reference MN ~1.3MB / PD ~1.6MB at full content;
       a Templates file under ~400KB with <4 scripts is almost certainly a clone-truncation).
  F4. all non-src <script> blocks pass `node --check`.
  F5. localStorage keys for subject-specific state follow the per-subject prefix convention
      (atimn / atipd / atiph / atimh) and do not leak across subjects.
```

The F3 size-bound is a coarse but useful early-warning. A Templates file under 400KB is suspicious unless it has very few cards; cross-check against MN/PD at the corresponding card count.

#### Origin of the issue
Likely cause: when MH Templates was originally cloned from PD, the source file was either truncated mid-edit or a copy-paste from a partial document missed the trailing scripts. The clone artifact persisted through every subsequent edit in this project because no edit touched the tail, and nothing in the previous verify-gate checked for tail completeness.

#### Updated push list for MH Templates ⚠️ HISTORICAL SNAPSHOT (frozen at the time of that session — for current counts/push status see the ⭐ MASTER CURRENT STATE block at top and `SESSION_VERIFICATION_CHECKLIST.md`)
The file now contains all the JS needed for clickable accordions, mode toggles, sidebar group expansion, hash navigation, and print. Re-upload `Elevated ATI MH Templates.html` once more to replace the structurally-incomplete version that may already be on GitHub.

### 27.8 Addendum — the JS depends on a modal+abbrTip HTML block (also missing in MH's clone)
After §27.7 ported the scripts into MH Templates, opening the file in a browser threw `Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'addEventListener')`. The MN scripts call `getElementById` on **7 modal-related ids** that didn't exist in MH's HTML:

```
exampleModal, exampleModalBody, exampleModalClose, exampleModalMeta,
exampleModalPrint, exampleModalTitle, abbrTip
```

In MN/PD, the modal/popup wrapper and abbreviation-tip element sit in the body **right before the first `<script>` tag** as a ~843-character HTML block:
```html
<div class="modal-overlay" id="exampleModal" aria-hidden="true">
  <div class="modal" role="dialog" aria-labelledby="exampleModalTitle">
    <div class="modal-header">
      <div class="modal-title-row">
        <div>
          <div class="modal-meta" id="exampleModalMeta">…</div>
          <h2 class="modal-title" id="exampleModalTitle">…</h2>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-actions">
          <button class="modal-print" id="exampleModalPrint" …>⎙</button>
          <button class="modal-close" id="exampleModalClose" …>×</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="modal-body" id="exampleModalBody"></div>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="abbr-tip" id="abbrTip"></div>
```

This block is the runtime target the scripts hook into. Without it, the bind step throws on the first `addEventListener` call and **all subsequent script registrations are aborted**, which explains why "nothing works" rather than just "the modal doesn't open."

#### Fix applied
Extracted the modal block from MN (843 chars between the `<div class="modal-overlay" id="exampleModal"…>` start and the first `<script>` tag) and inserted it into MH right before MH's first `<script>` tag. All 7 ids now resolve; JS parses; no duplicate ids.

#### Expanded file-completeness invariant (supersedes §27.7's F2)
```
FILE_COMPLETENESS_INVARIANTS (Templates files, updated):
  F1. file ends with </body></html>.
  F2. Two body-level prerequisite blocks present immediately before the scripts:
      (a) modal-overlay block with ids:
          exampleModal, exampleModalBody, exampleModalClose, exampleModalMeta,
          exampleModalPrint, exampleModalTitle
      (b) abbr-tip block with id: abbrTip
  F3. <script> count >= 4 non-src scripts (MN/PD canonical count).
  F4. file size within ~30% of MN/PD reference for comparable card count.
  F5. all non-src <script> blocks pass `node --check`.
  F6. localStorage keys follow the per-subject prefix convention
      (atimn / atipd / atiph / atimh).
  F7. After loading the file, the browser console reports NO uncaught errors.
      (This is the runtime version of F2 — catches missing-id-target issues
       that the static check might miss.)
```

F7 is the strongest invariant of the lot, since it catches the entire class of "scripts present but missing their HTML targets" bugs that the static checks can underspecify. It should be treated as the final gate.

#### Pattern note for clone-from-PD operations
When a Templates file is cloned from PD (or any other subject), the clone must include — in addition to the cards, sidebar, and accordions — the modal-overlay block, the abbrTip element, the closing `</body></html>` tags, and all `<script>` blocks. A 'clone from PD' that only copies the visible scaffold (cards + CSS) is structurally incomplete and will silently appear to work until the user clicks something interactive. Document the full tail-of-body required composition as the standard clone unit; a partial clone should fail the F2/F3 gate at write time.

### 27.9 Addendum — the ACTUAL root cause: templatePool needs N typed `<section>` children, properly closed, with modal OUTSIDE the pool
The §27.7 / §27.8 patches got the file to render statically but clicking a template still did nothing — and worse, no template would open at all. The cascade of "fix one, the next thing is broken" stopped here when the actual structural model the JS depends on was traced end-to-end.

#### The JS contract for templatePool (from MN/PD script[0])
```javascript
var pool = document.getElementById('templatePool');
document.querySelectorAll('.unit-accordion[data-template-id]').forEach(function(acc){
  var templateId = acc.getAttribute('data-template-id');
  var template = pool.querySelector('#' + templateId);  // ← per-type SECTION inside pool
  var body = acc.querySelector('.unit-body');
  if (!template || !body) return;
  var examples = template.querySelectorAll('.example-card');
  // …builds bullet list, then moves cards into body via appendChild…
});
```

The JS expects **one `<section>` per template type**, each `<section>` having the `data-template-id` value as its **`id`** (literally `id="basic-concept"`, `id="diagnostic-procedure"`, etc.), each containing **only its own type's example-cards**. The accordion-population step copies bullet-list metadata into the unit-body, then moves the actual cards out of the pool into the unit-body.

#### What was wrong in MH after §27.7–§27.8
The MH file had:
- A single `<section id="basic-concept" class="template-section">` containing **all 54 cards** regardless of type.
- That section **never closed** (no `</section>`).
- `<div id="templatePool">` never closed (no closing `</div>`).
- The modal-overlay + abbrTip blocks I had injected in §27.8 ended up **inside** the still-open template-pool — which has `.template-pool { display: none }` — so the modal was永-hidden no matter what JS did.

JS effect at page-load:
- Accordion `data-template-id="basic-concept"` finds `#basic-concept` → moves ALL 54 cards into the BC accordion (visible but mis-typed).
- All other accordions find `pool.querySelector('#diagnostic-procedure'|'#growth-development'|…)` → **null** → early return → empty bodies.
- Clicking any non-BC accordion shows nothing; clicking BC shows everything; clicking a sidebar link tries to open the modal which is hidden inside the pool → nothing visible.

#### The fix (§27.9)
Rebuilt the entire templatePool subtree:
```html
<div class="template-pool" id="templatePool">

  <div class="tpl-filter-panel" id="tplFilterPanel">…preserved verbatim…</div>

  <section id="basic-concept" class="template-section">
    <div class="example-card"…>…</div>  <!-- 13 BC cards -->
    …
  </section>

  <section id="diagnostic-procedure" class="template-section">
    <div class="example-card"…>…</div>  <!-- 4 DP cards -->
    …
  </section>

  <section id="growth-development" class="template-section">…</section>
  <section id="medication" class="template-section">…</section>
  <section id="nursing-skill" class="template-section">…</section>
  <section id="system-disorder" class="template-section">…</section>
  <section id="therapeutic-procedure" class="template-section">…</section>
  <section id="concept-analysis" class="template-section">…</section>

</div>  <!-- end templatePool — properly closed -->

<div class="modal-overlay" id="exampleModal">…</div>  <!-- OUTSIDE the pool -->
<div class="abbr-tip" id="abbrTip"></div>             <!-- OUTSIDE the pool -->

<script>…</script>  <!-- 4 scripts -->
</body></html>
```

Cards were grouped by type using the sidebar's `sb-tpl-group → sb-tpl-example` links as the authoritative card-to-type mapping. (The sidebar is the single source of truth for which type each card belongs to, because cards themselves carry no `data-template-id`.)

#### The final, complete file-completeness invariant (supersedes everything in §27.7/§27.8)
**For any Templates file, the verify-gate must assert all of the following — in tail-of-body order — before the closing tags:**

```
TEMPLATES_TAIL_STRUCTURE (in this exact order, no overlap):
  T1. <div class="template-pool" id="templatePool">
        T1a. <div class="tpl-filter-panel" id="tplFilterPanel">…</div>
        T1b. <section id="<tpl>" class="template-section">…cards…</section>
             for each <tpl> in CANONICAL_GROUPS, in canonical order
        T1c. (no other content)
      </div>  ← templatePool MUST close

  T2. <div class="modal-overlay" id="exampleModal">…</div>
      (with descendants: exampleModalBody, exampleModalClose, exampleModalMeta,
       exampleModalPrint, exampleModalTitle)

  T3. <div class="abbr-tip" id="abbrTip"></div>

  T4. <script>…</script> × N (N ≥ 4 for MN/PD pattern, all parse via `node --check`)

  T5. </body></html>

INVARIANTS_OVER_TAIL_STRUCTURE:
  T1.id="templatePool" appears exactly once.
  Each canonical type's <section id="<tpl>"> appears exactly once,
    in canonical order, and contains ONLY cards of that type
    (mapping derived from sidebar sb-tpl-example links).
  The card count inside each <section> matches the corresponding sb-tpl-count
    AND the unit-count target on the matching unit-accordion.
  Modal and abbrTip blocks sit OUTSIDE templatePool (display:none on pool
    would hide them otherwise).
  Scripts sit OUTSIDE templatePool.
```

#### Pattern note for future clone operations
A "clone Templates file from a working subject" operation is **incomplete** unless it copies the entire tail-of-body in T1–T5 order verbatim. Copying only the visible scaffold (header + sidebar + main accordions + cards) without the modal+abbrTip blocks AND without the templatePool wrapper AND without the scripts produces a file that **renders statically but crashes silently** when any interactive element is clicked. The clone operation should be defined as a single transactional copy of the full tail-of-body, with subject-specific storage key swaps applied as a post-step.

The lesson: when interactive UI behavior is "everything broken," check structural completeness of the tail-of-body before debugging script logic. A static document with valid HTML and valid JS can still be functionally inert if the script's target DOM scaffolding is missing.

### 27.10 Addendum — pre-existing stale-counts bug across MN, PD, Pharm Templates
Discovered while auditing PD for the same coverage issues we addressed in MH. PD's main-area accordion `unit-count` targets were all set to MN's old numbers (e.g., `0 / 40 studied` on System Disorder when PD actually has 116 SD cards). The same bug existed in Pharm and MN itself; only MH was correct, because §27.6 had rebuilt its accordion section from current sidebar counts.

#### Cause
The original PD and Pharm Templates files were cloned from MN. The clone correctly copied the 8 unit-accordion shells but kept the `0 / N studied` target values that were set when MN had a smaller content footprint. As cards were added to each subject over time, the sidebar `sb-tpl-count` values were updated by the card-add operations, but the corresponding main-area accordion `unit-count` targets were never updated, because the standard add-card operation only touched the sidebar surface.

This is the same dual-surface omission that §27.6 corrected for MH — sidebar updates without matching main-area-accordion updates leave the two structural surfaces out of sync.

#### Fix applied
For each of MN, PD, and Pharm: parsed `sb-tpl-count` from each sidebar group (the authoritative count, derived from actual `<a class="sb-tpl-example">` link entries), then regex-replaced the matching `unit-count" id="<tpl>-count">0 / N studied` value to match. All four subjects now satisfy the S4 invariant exactly:

```
S4 (verified across all 4 subjects after this fix):
  for each canonical template type:
    sb-tpl-count[data-tpl=X]
      == count(<a class="sb-tpl-example"> within that sidebar group)
      == accordion unit-count target [id="X-count"]
      == count(<div class="example-card"> inside <section id="X">)
```

#### Updated card-add operation invariant
Any card-add operation on a Templates file must update **three** numbers transactionally, not two:

```
ADD_CARD_TRANSACTION:
  1. Insert the card HTML inside <section id="<tpl>" class="template-section"> in templatePool.
  2. Append an <a class="sb-tpl-example"> link inside the matching sidebar group.
  3. Increment the sidebar group's <span class="sb-tpl-count"> value.
  4. Increment the matching <span class="unit-count" id="<tpl>-count">0 / N studied</span> N value.
  Steps 3 AND 4 must move together — if either moves alone, the file violates S4
  and the progress display misleads students.
```

The `tplgen.py` `add_new` generator should be updated to apply step 4 as part of the same operation, not as an after-the-fact patch.

#### Pre-existing-file remediation note
The mechanism in §27.10 should be run once on any Templates file whose history pre-dates the consolidated `add_new` (steps 3 + 4 together) — derive targets from sidebar, regex-update the unit-count display. This is mechanical, idempotent, and safe; if S4 is already satisfied, the operation is a no-op.

#### Student-facing impact (now resolved)
- PD: SD progress bar showed "0 of 40 studied" when there were actually 116 cards → students saw 8 to go after completing 40, when in reality 76 more remained.
- Pharm: Med showed "0 of 14 studied" when there are actually 93 — students could "complete" the bar at 14 and not realize they were 79 cards from done.
- MN: TP showed "0 of 14" when there are 20 cards; SD showed "0 of 40" when there are 60.

After the §27.10 fix all four files display accurate progress targets.

## PART 28 — PHARM POST-COMPLETION: DUPLICATION INCIDENT + VISUAL-RICHNESS/DENSITY AUDIT

### 28.1 Duplication incident (and the fix)
A compaction summary stated Pharm ch11-49 had "no expanded content-section pills," and an opening scan in the working session agreed (reported ch11-49 as empty). Both were **wrong**: a prior pass had already authored expanded content for ch11-49 — sections named `overview`, `agents`, `toxicity`, `selection`, etc. — **except ch11, ch20, and ch27**, which were genuinely empty.

Acting on the bad baseline, 14 "authoring" batches re-authored chapters that were already done, creating a **duplicate, thinner set of sections** (65 pills) in ch12-19, 21-26, and 28-42, alongside the pre-existing content. No prior content was lost; the duplicates simply sat on top.

**How it was caught:** the whole-file pill count jumped far above the running total (368 vs the expected ~204), and chapters never touched in-session (ch43-49) showed pills. **Lesson:** when a chapter you never edited contains content, the baseline is wrong — stop and re-derive the true starting state before continuing. A correct fix is to verify the real baseline first, not to trust a summary.

**Remediation:** removed only the in-session duplicate sections (matched by their specific id stems) from ch12-19/21-26/28-42, keeping the better pre-existing content; kept the legitimately-new content in the three empty chapters (ch11/20/27); left ch43-49 untouched. Added a matching `overview` section to ch11/20/27 for house-style parity. Result: **306 pills, no duplication, no within-chapter near-dups, all 49 chapters populated, JS clean.** Verify-gate asserted exact pill delta (−65), exercises unchanged (251), no leftover in-session sections in target chapters, no chapter emptied, no dup IDs.

### 28.2 Visual-richness / density audit (cross-book)
Triggered by the observation that Pharm reads as plain "white text inside a pill" while the other books use accent color, tables, and "pills within pills." Objective per-book counts:

| Book | pills | pills/tab | finding-grids | finding-cards | data-tables |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MN | 612 | 3.83 | 170 | 427 | 18 |
| PD | 574 | 3.30 | 0 | 0 | 46 |
| MH | 340 | 2.04 | 109 | 306 | 0 |
| Pharm | 306 | 2.12 | 111 | 210 | 0 |

**The "pills within pills" structure** = `finding-grid` containing `finding-card`s (each card has an accent-colored `<h4>` header) inside a `condition-block`. **Tables** = the defined `.data-table` component. Both render in the theme accent color, which is what makes a chapter look "colorful" rather than a plain `<ul>`.

**Within Pharm, the richness is not evenly distributed:**
- ch1-10 (original build): **107 finding-grids** — rich, pills-within-pills throughout.
- ch11/20/27 (filled later): 4 grids.
- pre-existing ch12-49: **0 grids** — entirely plain `<ul>`.

So the plainness spans ~38 of 49 chapters (all of ch11-49 except light grid use in ch11/20), the bulk being the earlier ch12-49 authoring. Pharm also has **zero data-tables** (vs MN 18, PD 46) and the lowest density alongside MH (~2.1 pills/tab vs MN/PD 3.3-3.8). The book is internally inconsistent: a rich ch1-10 followed by a plain ch11-49.

### 28.3 Styling standard going forward (all books)
- **Use `finding-grid` + `finding-card`** for any pill whose content has multiple facets (uses / complications / contraindications / interactions / nursing). Plain `<ul>` is acceptable only for genuinely single-facet pills. This is the "pills within pills" look and the primary source of accent color in a chapter.
- **Use `.data-table`** for comparative or reference data (drug-class comparisons, onset/peak/duration, lab ranges, schedules) — the styled, accent-themed table component. PD and MN rely on these heavily; Pharm currently has none despite many natural candidates (insulin onset/peak/duration, antidysrhythmic classes, diuretic classes, vaccine schedule).
- **Density target:** aim for the MN/PD range (~3+ pills per content tab) rather than ~2, where the source supports it — i.e., split broad single pills into per-drug-class pills with richer internal structure.
- **Consistency check** (recommended new gate): before declaring a book "complete," compare its grids/cards/tables/pills-per-tab against the others; a book that is internally inconsistent (rich early chapters, plain later ones) is not done.

### 28.4 Status ⚠️ HISTORICAL SNAPSHOT (frozen at the time of that session — for current counts/push status see the ⭐ MASTER CURRENT STATE block at top and `SESSION_VERIFICATION_CHECKLIST.md`)
- Pharm: **306 pills, 49 ch** — duplication resolved; content complete and faithful, but **visually plainer and less dense than MN/PD** in ch11-49. Candidate for a richness/density enrichment pass (convert plain-`<ul>` pills to finding-grids, add data-tables for comparative content, raise pills/tab) — to be done batch by batch with the verify-gate, never one-pass.
- MN 612, PD 574, MH 340 unaffected by this work.

## PART 29 — RICHNESS-CONVERSION RULEBOOK (HOLISTIC, PER-PILL) — *authoritative; read before any styling pass*

### 29.0 Why this part exists (the mistake it prevents)
During the richness pass on MN, conversion was done at the **tab level**: the "obvious" pills in a tab were turned into finding-cards/tables and single-category list pills were left as plain bullets. Result: a card-pill sitting directly next to a bare bullet-pill in the same tab — which the user correctly flagged as "out of place," and which looks **worse** than a tab where everything is uniformly plain. The fix and the permanent rule: **convert holistically, per pill, never half a tab.**

### 29.1 The unit of conversion is the PILL, not the tab
A tab is "done" only when **every** content pill in it is visually consistent. Detecting "plain tabs" (tabs with zero finding-grids) is insufficient — a tab can contain one finding-grid pill and several bare-list pills and still read as inconsistent. Before declaring any tab done, enumerate **all** its `condition-block` pills and confirm none is a bare `<ul>`/`<ol>` sitting beside a carded pill.

### 29.2 Per-pill decision tree (apply to every content pill)
1. **Two or more natural facets** (uses/complications, advantages/disadvantages, avoid/encourage, maternal/fetal, before/after) → `finding-grid` with 2+ `finding-card`s. If the facets currently live in two *separate* pills, **merge them into one pill** with a 2-card grid (approved rule; see §29.4).
2. **Tabular / sequential / label→value data** (timelines, onset-peak-duration, drug→dose, infection→finding, term→definition) → `<table class="data-table">` with a `<caption>` and `<thead>`.
3. **Single-category bullet list** (one coherent list, no natural split) → wrap in a `finding-grid` containing **one** `finding-card`. The card's `<h4>` must be a **meaningful facet label that adds information**, never a restatement of the pill's `<h3>` (established convention: "Physical assessment findings" → h4 "Evaluation criteria"; "Fundal assessment technique" → h4 "Documentation"). Single-card grids are valid and render full-width.
4. **Short prose paragraph pill** (no list) → **REVISED canon (§32 Pattern D, post-Batch D):** never leave a pill body as a bare `<p>` alone — pair the paragraph with an accent-labeled inner card (`kb-card` with `<h4>`, `finding-grid`, or `data-table`). User feedback (Image 3, Nägele's rule) confirmed bare-paragraph pills feel "out of place" next to richer pills. See §32.3 Pattern D for the canonical skeleton. (A paragraph followed by a list → keep the paragraph, card the list.)
5. **Header tag/badge** (`<span class="condition-tag">`): add to a pill's header when there is a single key takeaway (e.g., "Penicillin G first-line", "<3/hr or none ×12 hr → notify", a "flag" tag for danger). Tags add header accent color but do **not** by themselves fix a bare body — a tagged bare list is still a bare list.

### 29.3 Components & their meaning (the "color" the user wants)
- **`finding-grid` + `finding-card`** = "pills inside pills": cards with accent-colored `<h4>` headers. Primary source of in-pill color. `finding-grid` is `auto-fit minmax(240px,1fr)`; 1 card → full width, 2 → side by side.
- **`data-table`** = the accent-themed reference table (caption + thead). Use for comparative/sequential data. Heavily used in MN/PD; under-used elsewhere.
- **`condition-tag`** = header badge (accent; add `flag` class for danger/red emphasis).
- All of `finding-grid`, `finding-card`, `data-table`, `condition-tag`, `kb-card`, `trimester-grid/card`, `ati-deep` are **defined in every book's CSS** — verified. A pill rendering as plain white text is almost always a bare `<ul>`, not an undefined class.

### 29.4 Merge rule for contrast pairs (approved)
When two adjacent pills form a natural contrast (Avoid/Encourage, Advantages/Disadvantages, Lactating/Non-lactating), **merge into one pill** with a 2-card `finding-grid`. This reduces pill count by 1 for that tab but produces the richer, denser look. Confirm no other code references the removed pill id before merging (grep the id; flashcard anchors use the *section* id, not the pill id, so removal is normally safe).

### 29.5 Mandatory verify-gate for every styling write  (richness-pass application of ⭐ §23.4 CORE)
The shared CORE checks (⭐ §23.4) apply; for restyling writes use the word-preservation form of check #1, plus these richness-specific additions. Abort the write unless ALL pass:
- **Word-preservation:** `set(words(old_block)) - set(words(new_block)) == ∅` (tags collapsed, lowercased, alphanumeric tokens). This proves pure restructuring — no text added/removed. Note: it is *strict* — a verb-inflection change (e.g., "warranting"→"warrant") trips it; preserve original wording or accept the flag and fix.
- **Pill-count delta = expected** (0 normally; −1 per merge).
- **No duplicate `condition-block` ids.**
- **No bare-list pills remain** in any tab touched (re-scan: `<ul>`/`<ol>` present AND no `finding-grid`/`data-table` in the pill).
- **JS: 0 errors** (`node --check` on every non-src `<script>`).

### 29.6 Batch discipline (per the standing project rule)
Slow but sure — small batches (one chapter or a few tabs), present after each, check in. Never one-pass across many chapters. Quality and the user's review are the optimization target, not throughput. The word-gate catches *mechanical* loss only; it cannot catch a fact placed in a misleading group or an overstated badge — only the user's review can, which is why batches stay small and reviewable.  (⭐ §23.5)

### 29.7 Scope reality (cross-suite)
Making every bullet-list pill consistent is large: per-pill, it is more than the ~386 "plain tabs" figure — it is essentially every single-category list in all four books. Track progress per chapter; do not declare a book "done" until a per-pill scan shows zero bare-list pills beside carded pills.

### 29.8 Retrofit note
MN ch2, ch3, ch5, ch8 were converted at the tab level (pre-rule) and contain bare-list pills next to carded pills; they are being retrofitted per §29.1-29.2. ch4 was the first chapter fixed holistically and is the reference example.

## PART 30 — GLOBAL CSS RICHNESS BASELINE (Phase 1) — *supersedes the per-pill-everywhere plan of PART 29*

### 30.0 Why this part exists (two more missed categories + a better strategy)
The per-pill conversion of PART 29 had a hidden flaw: the "bare-list" scan matched only the literal tag `<ul>`, so it **silently skipped**:
- **`flag-list`** lists (`<ul class="flag-list">` / `<ol class="flag-list">`) — 123 in MN alone — which render with red bullet markers but no card box (read as "plain white text" to the user).
- **`kb-card` lists** — ~101 in MN — whose `<h4>` was **unstyled** (`.kb-card h4` was never defined), so the header rendered plain white instead of accent-colored.

So chapters marked "fully consistent" under PART 29 still contained plain-reading content. Hand-converting every list across all four books (1000+ pills, ≥3 list categories) is slow and proved easy to under-scope. **The better strategy is CSS-first.**

### 30.1 The insight
The "plain" look = a list lacking (a) a **card box** and (b) an **accent header label**. The header label needs a real `<h4>` element (structure, per-pill). But the **card box can be applied globally via CSS** to every list at once. So:
- **Phase 1 (global CSS):** guarantee a consistent boxed-card baseline for *every* list, all books, zero content risk.
- **Phase 2 (targeted structure):** add labeled finding-cards / data-tables only where grouping adds meaning (contrast pairs, multi-facet lists, tabular data). Optional polish, not mandatory.

User decision (approved): the Phase 1 baseline is **sufficient for single-topic lists**; Phase 2 is reserved for multi-facet/contrast/tabular pills only. Do not force a sub-label onto a single-topic list (it would merely echo the pill title).

### 30.2 The two CSS additions (applied to all four books)
**(a) Fix the unstyled kb-card header** — clone each book's own `.finding-card h4` rule onto `.kb-card h4` (so it matches that book's theme accent):
```
.kb-card h4{ /* same props as that book's .finding-card h4 */
  font-family:'DM Sans',sans-serif;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;
  text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:0.12em;
  color:var(--accent2);margin:0 0 8px;
}
```
**(b) Phase 1 list-boxing** — DIRECT-CHILD selectors only, so lists already inside `.finding-card` / `.kb-card` / `.ati-deep` / `.trimester-card` are NOT touched (no double-boxing):
```
.condition-block > ul,
.condition-block > ol{
  background:var(--surface2);border:1px solid var(--border-soft);
  border-radius:10px;padding:14px 18px 14px 34px;margin:14px 0 0;
  font-size:13.5px;color:var(--text2);line-height:1.55;
}
.condition-block > ul li{margin-bottom:5px}
.condition-block > ol li{margin-bottom:5px}
.condition-block > ul li:last-child,
.condition-block > ol li:last-child{margin-bottom:0}
.condition-block > ul.flag-list,
.condition-block > ol.flag-list{
  border-color:var(--nonreassuring);box-shadow:inset 3px 0 0 var(--nonreassuring);
}
.condition-block > ul ul,.condition-block > ul ol,
.condition-block > ol ul,.condition-block > ol ol{
  background:none;border:0;border-radius:0;padding:6px 0 0 18px;margin:0;box-shadow:none}
```
Insert both right after the book's `.finding-card h4{…}` rule. All four books define `.finding-card h4` and the vars `--surface2 --border-soft --text2 --accent2 --nonreassuring`, so the same block themes itself per book (MN amber, PD sky, MH lime, Pharm orange). Verify `node --check` on every non-src `<script>` = 0 after insert.

### 30.3 Why direct-child (`>`) matters
The per-pill finding-cards built in MN ch1-9 hold their lists inside `.finding-card`, i.e. `.finding-grid > .finding-card > ul` — NOT a direct child of `.condition-block`. So `.condition-block > ul` cannot match them and there is no double-boxing. The same protects kb-card and ati-deep lists. This is the load-bearing detail; if the `>` is dropped, everything double-boxes.

### 30.4 Status after Phase 1
All four books now render every in-pill list as a themed card box; flag-lists keep a red inset stripe; kb-card headers are accent-colored. No "plain white text" remains anywhere. MN ch1-9 additionally have hand-labeled finding-cards/tables (the "premium" Phase-2 example). Phase 2 elsewhere is optional and selective.

### 30.5 Standing rule going forward
New chapters/pills inherit the baseline automatically (any `<ul>`/`<ol>` placed directly in a `condition-block` is boxed by CSS). Author normally; reach for an explicit `finding-grid`+`finding-card` only when a pill has ≥2 meaningful facets, or a `data-table` for tabular data. Never wrap a single-topic list in a one-card grid just to add a header — the baseline already styles it.
