No visible change today (their static badges were already correct) — purely future-proofing for their upcoming enrichment passes.

**MH STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE (CORRECTED — MH is NEWER, not older):** Initial read mischaracterized `Elevated ATI MH Templates.html` (334 KB) as "older/simpler." On closer inspection it uses a MORE ADVANCED architecture than Pharm/MN/PD: an **accordion + hidden template-pool** system. The 8 template types render as collapsible `unit-accordion` widgets (own headers, ATI page labels A1/A3/…, progress bars, "0 / N studied" counts); the `<section>` blocks live inside a hidden `<div class="template-pool" id="templatePool">` and are MOVED into the accordion bodies by JS on page load. There is intentionally NO `template-banner`/`status-badge` in the visible flow — the accordion headers provide heading + count UI (driven by MH's own progress JS). 

**A brief retrofit attempt (wrapping MH sections in template-banner/status-badge) was made and then REVERTED** — it would have injected redundant banners into pooled content that JS relocates. `syncSectionBadges()` is NOT applicable and was NOT added to MH. MH left untouched (61 examples, accordion architecture intact). 

**Note:** MH has 1 pre-existing unclosed `<div>` in its pool/layout markup (browsers auto-correct; structurally inherited) — left as-is; optional separate HTML-validity cleanup if ever desired. **Forward-looking consistency question is the REVERSE of what was first assumed:** whether Pharm/MN/PD should eventually adopt MH's accordion+filter UX — not whether MH should be downgraded to their static-banner style.

Per-chapter: survey ATI Mental Health PDF first → cross-check anchor in `Elevated ATI MH Book.html` → propose table → approve → insert before first fc-ch(N+1) → validate (count + node --check + 0 dupes + no `\u`) → update §41.5 tracker → present_files. Book-faithful; reframe/swap if source lacks support.

## §41.3 SAFETY NOTE for sensitive MH chapters  (operational subset of ⭐ §26.3 — the canonical framework)
ch19 (Eating Disorders), ch30 (Suicide), ch31 (Anger), ch32 (Family/Community Violence), ch33 (Sexual Assault): keep all flashcard content **educational/clinical only** — NO methods, NO specific numbers (calories/weights for ED; means for suicide), NO step-by-step that could enable harm. Focus on nursing assessment, therapeutic response, safety planning principles, and resources.

# PART 42 — SESSION LEARNINGS LOG (PD Flashcards completion + MH kickoff) [2026-06-17]

Cross-cutting lessons from completing PD Flashcards (PART 40) that generalize to MH Flashcards (PART 41) and all future per-chapter enrichment. Per-chapter specifics live in §40.0 and the §40.5 / §41.5 trackers.

## §42.1 — Survey snapshot can lag a same-turn insert
Twice (PD ch31, and watch for it generally) the pre-insert survey output reflected a state from *before* a prior insert in the same logical step, making proposed cards look "new" when they already existed. **Mitigation:** the authoritative check is always the post-insert `re.findall(r"\{\s*id:\s*'([^']+)'", fc)` dup scan + per-chapter count, NOT the survey. If the survey shows a card you're about to add already present, re-read the live file before assuming a collision.

## §42.2 — Off-topic uniform-baseline artifacts are common
The uniform 13-cards/chapter baseline seeded several chapters with cards belonging to *other* topics (PD ch24: 5 newborn-assessment cards; ch34: 3 infectious-disease cards; ch41: 1 neonatal-RDS card). **Policy applied:** leave them as-is (do not expand or build on a mismatch), add on-topic cards alongside, and log the artifact in the tracker Notes column. Expect the same in MH — flag, don't silently "fix".

## §42.3 — Book-faithfulness swap discipline
When a planned card duplicates an existing one or lacks Book support, SWAP it for a Book-verified substitute rather than dropping silently. Logged examples: PD ch2 (cuff-size → NHBPEP bp-standards), ch9 (codeine omitted — already carded ch8), ch21 (chelation → acute-chest syndrome). Always re-verify the substitute against the Book before insert.

## §42.4 — Final-array-element comma handling
The last STARTER_DECK element (immediately before `];`) has NO trailing comma. When appending to the FINAL chapter (PD ch44, MH ch33), the insert must (a) add a comma to the previously-last element and (b) leave the new last card comma-less. Mid-array inserts don't hit this. `node --check` catches a mistake here.

## §42.5 — Batch sizing heuristic (validated across 44 PD chapters)
Scale batch to chapter size/under-cardedness, not a fixed number:
- **5–6 cards:** very large or heavily under-carded chapters (PD ch20 70 KB, ch42 69 KB, ch1/2/3 foundational).
- **3–4 cards:** typical chapters.
- **2 cards:** already-thorough chapters (PD ch31, ch37).
Average across PD was ~4/chapter (572 → 747 = +175 / 44). MH starts uniform 13/chapter (430 total) — expect a similar +3 to +5 average.

## §42.6 — Sensitive-content guardrail (carries into MH §41.3; defers to ⭐ §26.3 canonical framework)
For eating disorders, suicide/self-harm, violence, and sexual assault content: educational/clinical framing only — assessment findings, therapeutic nursing response, safety-planning *principles*, resources. NO methods, NO specific numbers (calories/weights, means). PD ch44 handled this way; MH ch19/30/31/32/33 require the same care.

## §42.7 — Unicode glyph discipline (unchanged, reconfirmed)
Build cards with `\uXXXX` in Python, then replace to literal glyphs before writing (–—→°≥≤₂↑↓·±β etc.), and assert `backslash-u remaining: False` after every insert. Genuine escaped apostrophes (`child\'s`, `Prehn\'s`) must match raw bytes. PD/MH Flashcards use PLAIN single quotes; `repr()` shows them escaped — do not add backslashes.

### §47.63 AMS Phase 3BG Unit 12 Book Content - Chapter 83

Date: 2026-06-28

Public file edited:

- `Elevated ATI AMS Book.html`

Chapter authored:

- Ch83 `Complications of Diabetes Mellitus`

Source verification:

- Private source only: ATI RN Adult Medical Surgical Nursing Review Module, Edition 11, Unit 12, Ch83, pages 555-558 in the module text.
- Source-supported content scope used:
  - DKA as rapid hyperglycemia with ketones and metabolic acidosis.
  - HHS as profound hyperglycemia with hyperosmolar dehydration and absent ketosis.
  - DKA risk triggers including missed/reduced insulin, untreated type 1 diabetes, infection, illness, and stress hormone response.
  - HHS risk triggers including older adulthood, inadequate fluid intake, kidney impairment, MI, stroke, sepsis, glucocorticoids, thiazide diuretics, phenytoin, beta blockers, and calcium channel blockers.
  - Expected findings for both conditions, DKA-specific ketone/acidosis findings, and HHS neurologic/osmolarity findings.
  - Serial labs: glucose, sodium, potassium, BUN/creatinine, ketones, osmolarity, and ABGs.
  - Nursing care: frequent vital signs, dehydration assessment, isotonic then maintenance fluids, IV regular insulin, dextrose addition near 250 mg/dL, potassium replacement safeguards, cardiac monitoring, bicarbonate for severe acidosis, and HHS neurologic monitoring.
  - Older-adult illness teaching, hydration, medical alert identification, sick-day glucose/ketone monitoring, and provider-call thresholds.
  - ATI-supported Basic Concept ALS for DKA plan of care and five ATI-aligned application exercises.

### 47.96 - AMS Unit 8 Renal Practice Expansion (2026-06-28)

Reason for batch:

- The current approved recommendation was a small, source-verified AMS Unit 8 renal expansion after live QA passed for Unit 5 hematologic practice. This pass targeted learner-facing renal safety patterns that are easy to confuse on ATI-style questions: contrast/metformin precautions, kidney-biopsy bleeding risk, dialysis access protection, postdialysis complications, disequilibrium syndrome, and peritoneal dialysis infection/flow/metabolic concerns. No quota-based cards were added.

Public files edited:

- `Elevated ATI AMS Hub.html`
- `Elevated ATI AMS Templates.html`
- `Elevated ATI AMS Flashcards.html`

ATI source support used:

- Private ATI RN Adult Medical Surgical Nursing Review Module, Edition 11, Ch 56 Renal Diagnostic Procedures:
  - Blood creatinine/BUN/urinalysis patterns, early-morning and 24-hr urine collection teaching, creatinine clearance as a GFR measure, and urine culture/sensitivity after leukocyte esterase/nitrite findings.
  - Excretory urography iodine-contrast preparation, allergy/asthma screening, BUN/creatinine checks, metformin withholding, hydration after contrast, and contrast-related kidney injury risk.
  - Kidney biopsy preprocedure coagulation review and postprocedure hemorrhage monitoring, including vital signs, dressing/urine assessment, Hgb/Hct, and pain.
- Private ATI RN Adult Medical Surgical Nursing Review Module, Edition 11, Ch 57 Hemodialysis and Peritoneal Dialysis:
  - Dialysis functions and limitations, hemodialysis indications, AV fistula/graft access assessment and access-arm restrictions, medication/lab/weight checks, heparin-related bleeding precautions, postdialysis hypovolemia/bleeding/infection/disequilibrium monitoring, and access-site reporting.
  - Disequilibrium syndrome cues and safety logic after rapid BUN/fluid-volume changes.
  - Peritoneal dialysis surgical asepsis, dialysate glucose monitoring, inflow/outflow expectations, cloudy/opaque effluent as an early peritonitis cue, wet dressing/leakage/access-site infection concerns, protein loss, hyperglycemia, and poor inflow/outflow interventions.
